translation: アレン夫妻は若い友人を手放すのを残念がった。彼女の上機嫌と明るさは彼女を大切な話し相手にしてくれていたし、彼女を楽しませているうちに夫妻自身の楽しみもいつのまにか増していたのである。
parts: whose good humour and cheerfulness had made her a valuable companion, and in the promotion of whose enjoyment their own had been gently increased
point: to lose ~ を目的語と見たり、関係詞節の whose good humour ... made her a valuable companion（SVOC）を判定したりしやすい。to lose は sorry の原因を表す修飾語。Mr. and Mrs. Allen were sorry で第2文型。
explanation: Mr. and Mrs. Allen＝sorry の関係。SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: ノーサンガー・アビー

text: An attempt at concealment had been her first instinctive movement on perceiving him, yet she could scarcely hope to have escaped his eye; and when her friend, who with an apologizing look darted hastily by her, had joined and disappeared with him, she ran for safety to her own room, and, locking herself in, believed that she should never have courage to go down again.
target: An attempt at concealment had been her first instinctive movement on perceiving him
translation: 隠れようとするのが、彼の姿を認めたときの彼女の本能的な最初の動きだったが、彼の目を逃れられたとはとても思えなかった。そして、申し訳なさそうな顔で彼女のそばを急いで通り過ぎた友人が彼と合流して一緒に姿を消すと、彼女は自分の部屋へ逃げこみ、鍵をかけて閉じこもって、もう二度と下へ降りていく勇気など出ないだろうと思った。
point: 後半の locking herself in（分詞構文）、to have escaped、courage to go down などに目を奪われやすい。また on perceiving him の him を目的語と見る誤りもある。An attempt had been her first movement で第2文型。
explanation: An attempt at concealment＝her first instinctive movement の関係。SVC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: ノーサンガー・アビー

text: Between the two sections of his flock he was often the only link, and it was his avowed custom to select those of his migratory sheep who seemed worthy, and give them a few hours in the pastures of the permanent.
target: it was his avowed custom to select those of his migratory sheep who seemed worthy, and give them a few hours in the pastures of the permanent
translation: 群れの二つの集団のあいだで、彼はしばしば唯一のつなぎ役だった。渡り歩く羊たちのうちふさわしいと思える者を選び、定住組の牧草地で数時間を過ごさせてやるのが、彼の公言している習慣だった。
parts: to select those of his migratory sheep who seemed worthy, and give them a few hours in the pastures of the permanent
point: 真主語の to select those ... and give them a few hours（SVOO）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。これは形式主語 it の中身。it は形式主語で、it＝his avowed custom の第2文型。
explanation: it（＝to select ...）＝his avowed custom の関係。SVC。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: It was pleasant, too, to fling wide the windows, pinching the fingers in unfamiliar fastenings, to lean out into sunshine with beautiful hills and trees and marble churches opposite, and close below, the Arno, gurgling against the embankment of the road.
translation: 窓を大きく開け放つのも楽しかった。慣れない留め金に指をはさみながら、日差しの中へ身を乗り出すと、向かいには美しい丘や木々や大理石の教会が見え、すぐ下ではアルノ川が道の土手に当たってごぼごぼと音を立てていた。
parts: to fling wide the windows, pinching the fingers in unfamiliar fastenings, to lean out into sunshine with beautiful hills and trees and marble churches opposite, and close below, the Arno, gurgling against the embankment of the road
point: 真主語の中の fling wide the windows（目的語が長いため wide が前に出た SVOC）や pinching the fingers（分詞構文）が目立ち、第5文型を選びやすい。これは形式主語 It の中身。It＝pleasant の第2文型。
explanation: It（＝to fling ... / to lean out ...）＝pleasant。SVC。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: She was glad when the gentlemen came, not merely because she caught her father’s eye to brighten her sleepiness up; but because she could listen to something larger and grander than the petty interests which the ladies had been talking about.
translation: 紳士たちがやってきたとき、彼女はうれしかった。父と目が合って眠気を吹き飛ばせたからというだけではない。婦人たちが話していたつまらない関心事よりも大きく堂々としたことに耳を傾けることができたからだ。
parts: when the gentlemen came, not merely because she caught her father’s eye to brighten her sleepiness up; but because she could listen to something larger and grander than the petty interests which the ladies had been talking about
point: to brighten her sleepiness up を目的語と見たり、関係詞節 which the ladies had been talking about に気を取られたりしやすい。to brighten は目的・結果の不定詞、because 節も修飾語。She was glad で第2文型。
explanation: She＝glad の関係。when 以下は時の M。SVC。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: Her father’s lips moved after her, repeating the well-known texts as her words suggested them; it was terrible to see the patient struggling effort to obtain the resignation which he had not strength to take into his heart as part of himself.
target: it was terrible to see the patient struggling effort to obtain the resignation which he had not strength to take into his heart as part of himself
translation: 父の唇は彼女のあとを追って動き、彼女の言葉に誘われるまま聞き慣れた聖句を繰り返していた。心に受け入れて自分のものにする力がない諦めを得ようとして、辛抱強くもがくその努力を見るのは、むごいことだった。
parts: to see the patient struggling effort to obtain the resignation which he had not strength to take into his heart as part of himself
point: 真主語の to see the patient struggling effort が知覚動詞＋O＋分詞（SVOC）に見えて、第5文型を選びやすい。実は struggling は effort を修飾する現在分詞。to see 以下は形式主語 it の中身。it＝terrible の第2文型。
explanation: it（＝to see ...）＝terrible。SVC。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: She was thankful to have been a Dodson, and to have one child who took after her own family, at least in his features and complexion, in liking salt and in eating beans, which a Tulliver never did.
translation: 彼女はドッドソン家に生まれたことをありがたく思い、少なくとも顔立ちや顔色、塩好きなところや豆を食べるところ――タリヴァー家の者は決してしなかったことだ――では自分の一族に似た子を一人持てたことを感謝していた。
parts: and to have one child who took after her own family, at least in his features and complexion, in liking salt and in eating beans, which a Tulliver never did
point: to have been a Dodson や to have one child を目的語と見て第3文型を選びやすい。これらは thankful の理由を表す不定詞。who took after her own family なども修飾語。She was thankful で第2文型。
explanation: She＝thankful の関係。SVC。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: That was fortunate in some respects, as labourers might be too ignorant to understand the propriety of her wanting to go to Dunlow Common; yet it would have been better if she could have met some one who would tell her the way without wanting to know anything about her private business.
target: That was fortunate in some respects, as labourers might be too ignorant to understand the propriety of her wanting to go to Dunlow Common
translation: それはある意味では幸運だった。労働者たちは無知すぎて、彼女がダンロウ・コモンへ行きたがるのももっともだということがわからないかもしれなかったからだ。とはいえ、彼女の私的な用事を何も知ろうとせずに道を教えてくれる人に会えたなら、そのほうがよかっただろう。
parts: as labourers might be too ignorant to understand the propriety of her wanting to go to Dunlow Common
point: 後半の who would tell her the way（SVOO）や without wanting to know に引っぱられやすい。also as 以下は理由を表す節。That was fortunate で、That＝fortunate の第2文型。
explanation: That＝fortunate の関係。as 以下は理由の M。SVC。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: Philip had been right when he told her that she knew nothing of renunciation; she had thought it was quiet ecstasy; she saw it face to face now,—that sad, patient, loving strength which holds the clue of life,—and saw that the thorns were forever pressing on its brow.
target: Philip had been right when he told her that she knew nothing of renunciation
translation: 彼女は諦めについて何も知らない、と言ったフィリップは正しかった。彼女はそれを静かな恍惚だと思っていた。いま彼女はそれと正面から向き合った――命の糸をつかむ、あの悲しく、辛抱強く、愛に満ちた強さと――そして、その額にいつも棘が食いこんでいることを知ったのだった。
parts: when he told her that she knew nothing of renunciation
point: when 節の told her that ~（SVOO）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。これは時の副詞節。Philip had been right で、Philip＝right の第2文型。
explanation: Philip＝right の関係。SVC。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: Mrs. Penniman had no appetite whatever for conversation with Mrs. Montgomery, whose acquaintance she made no trouble to cultivate; and the effect of this alarming forecast of her niece’s destiny was to make her think it indeed a thousand pities that Mr. Townsend’s generous nature should be embittered.
target: the effect of this alarming forecast of her niece’s destiny was to make her think it indeed a thousand pities that Mr. Townsend’s generous nature should be embittered
translation: ペニマン夫人はモンゴメリー夫人と話したいとはまったく思わず、知り合いになろうと骨を折ることもしなかった。そして姪の行く末についてのこの不吉な予言を聞いた結果、タウンゼンド氏の寛大な性分がすさんでしまうのは本当に残念でたまらない、と思うようになった。
parts: of this alarming forecast of her niece’s destiny
to make her think it indeed a thousand pities that Mr. Townsend’s generous nature should be embittered
point: 補語の不定詞 to make her think it a thousand pities that ~ の中に使役の SVOC と形式目的語の SVOC が入れ子になっていて、第5文型を選びやすい。不定詞全体は補語。the effect was to make ~ の第2文型。
explanation: the effect＝to make her think ... の関係。SVC。
note: 補語の不定詞の内側には SVOC が二重に入っているが、文型は主節の was で判定する。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ
workJa: ワシントン・スクエア

text: It was appalling to see her quietly moving forward with her plans, not bitter or excitable, neither asserting innocence nor confessing guilt, merely desiring freedom and the company of those who would not blame her.
translation: 彼女が静かに計画を進めていくのを見るのは、ぞっとするほどだった。苦々しくも興奮してもおらず、無実を言い立てるでも罪を告白するでもなく、ただ自由と、自分を責めない人々との交わりを望んでいるだけなのだった。
parts: to see her quietly moving forward with her plans, not bitter or excitable, neither asserting innocence nor confessing guilt, merely desiring freedom and the company of those who would not blame her
point: 真主語の to see her quietly moving forward（see O doing の知覚構文、SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これは形式主語 It の中身。It＝appalling の第2文型。
explanation: It（＝to see ...）＝appalling。SVC。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: The one moment of time which was long enough to bring me to that conclusion was also the moment which showed me a means of baffling his precautions—or, in other words, of hearing what he and Sir Percival said to each other, without the risk of descending at all into the lower regions of the house.
translation: その結論に達するのにちょうど足りるだけのその一瞬は、同時に、彼の用心の裏をかく手段――言いかえれば、館の下の階へ降りていく危険を冒さずに、彼とパーシヴァル卿が交わす言葉を聞く手段――を私に示してくれた瞬間でもあった。
parts: which was long enough to bring me to that conclusion

the moment which showed me a means of baffling his precautions—or, in other words, of hearing what he and Sir Percival said to each other, without the risk of descending at all into the lower regions of the house
point: 補語の moment を修飾する which showed me a means of baffling ~（SVOO）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。また主語の moment にも関係詞節がつき長い。moment＝the moment の第2文型。
explanation: The one moment＝the moment の関係。SVC。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: The plan which had now occurred to me was to get out at my sitting-room window on to this roof, to creep along noiselessly till I reached that part of it which was immediately over the library window, and to crouch down between the flower-pots, with my ear against the outer railing.
translation: そのとき思いついた計画は、居間の窓からこの屋根に出て、図書室の窓の真上にあたるところまで音を立てずに這っていき、植木鉢のあいだにかがんで、外側の手すりに耳を押し当てる、というものだった。
parts: which had now occurred to me

to get out at my sitting-room window on to this roof, to creep along noiselessly till I reached that part of it which was immediately over the library window, and to crouch down between the flower-pots, with my ear against the outer railing
point: 補語の不定詞 to get out / to creep / to crouch down が3つ並び、その中に till I reached ~ などがあるので、動詞を見誤りやすい。不定詞はまとめて補語。The plan was to ~ の第2文型。
explanation: The plan＝to get out ... の関係。SVC。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: Phœbe’s Indian cakes were the sweetest offering of all,—in their hue befitting the rustic altars of the innocent and golden age,—or, so brightly yellow were they, resembling some of the bread which was changed to glistening gold when Midas tried to eat it.
translation: フィービーのとうもろこしパンこそ、すべての供え物の中でいちばん甘いものだった。その色合いは、無垢な黄金時代の素朴な祭壇にふさわしく――あるいは、あまりに明るい黄色なので、ミダスが食べようとすると輝く金に変わってしまったというあのパンに似ていた。
parts: in their hue befitting the rustic altars of the innocent and golden age
or, so brightly yellow were they, resembling some of the bread which was changed to glistening gold when Midas tried to eat it
point: 倒置の挿入 so brightly yellow were they や関係詞節 which was changed to glistening gold（受動態）に気を取られやすい。befitting も分詞。Phœbe's Indian cakes were the sweetest offering で第2文型。
explanation: Phœbe’s Indian cakes＝the sweetest offering の関係。SVC。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン
work: The House of the Seven Gables

text: Look here, Padrona, I am the same man who came ashore one evening and sat down in the thatched ranche you lived in at that time on the other side of the town and told you all about himself.
target: I am the same man who came ashore one evening and sat down in the thatched ranche you lived in at that time on the other side of the town and told you all about himself
translation: いいかい、パドローナ、俺はあの晩上陸して、そのころあんたが住んでいた町の向こう側の草ぶきの小屋に腰を下ろし、自分のことを洗いざらい話した、あの同じ男なんだぜ。
parts: who came ashore one evening and sat down in the thatched ranche you lived in at that time on the other side of the town and told you all about himself
point: 関係詞節の told you all about himself（SVOO）や、前置詞 in が後ろに残る you lived in に目を奪われやすい。それは man を修飾する部分。I am the same man で、I＝man の第2文型。
explanation: I＝the same man の関係。SVC。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: I held up a screen, and did not look, and, as she said, she tried not to make the noise very offensive; but now that she was left alone, she seemed quite horrified when I begged her to remain with me in the warm dining-parlour, and enjoy her orange as she liked best.
target: now that she was left alone, she seemed quite horrified when I begged her to remain with me in the warm dining-parlour, and enjoy her orange as she liked best
translation: 私はついたてをかざして見ないようにし、彼女も言うとおり、音がなるべく耳ざわりにならないよう気をつけていた。けれど一人残されたいまとなっては、暖かい食堂で私と一緒にいて、好きなようにオレンジを召し上がってくださいと頼むと、彼女はすっかり震え上がったようだった。
parts: now that she was left alone
when I begged her to remain with me in the warm dining-parlour, and enjoy her orange as she liked best
point: when 以下の begged her to remain ... and enjoy ~（beg O to do、SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。now that 節も修飾語。she seemed quite horrified で、she＝horrified の第2文型。
explanation: seem は be と同じく主語の状態を表す動詞。she＝quite horrified の関係。SVC。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: The great reason with my own personal self for not letting you court me is, that I do not feel the things a woman ought to feel who consents to walk with you with the meaning of being your wife.
translation: 私自身があなたに言い寄るのを許さない大きな理由はね、妻になるつもりであなたと一緒に歩くことに同意する女が感じるはずのことを、私が感じていないということなの。
parts: with my own personal self for not letting you court me
that I do not feel the things a woman ought to feel who consents to walk with you with the meaning of being your wife
point: 補語の that 節の中の letting you court me（let O do）や関係詞節 who consents to walk with you に気を取られやすい。that 節全体が補語。The great reason is that ~ の第2文型。
explanation: The great reason＝that I do not feel ... の関係。SVC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: It was very pleasant to Thomasin, when she had carried the child to some lonely place, to give her a little private practice on the green turf and shepherd’s-thyme, which formed a soft mat to fall headlong upon them when equilibrium was lost.
translation: 子どもをどこか人けのない場所へ連れていき、緑の芝草とイブキジャコウソウの上でこっそり歩く練習をさせてやるのは、トマシンにとってとても楽しいことだった。その草は、よろけて頭から倒れたときのやわらかな敷物になってくれたのである。
parts: when she had carried the child to some lonely place
to give her a little private practice on the green turf and shepherd’s-thyme, which formed a soft mat to fall headlong upon them when equilibrium was lost
point: 真主語の to give her a little private practice（SVOO）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。間に when 節も挟まる。これは形式主語 It の中身。It＝pleasant の第2文型。
explanation: It（＝to give ...）＝very pleasant。SVC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: All he asked Charles Gould (whom he took for a mysterious and official person) to do for him was to remind the supreme Government--El Gobierno supreme--of a pension (amounting to about a dollar a month) to which he believed himself entitled.
translation: 彼がチャールズ・グールド（彼はこの人を謎めいた役人だと思いこんでいた）に頼んだのはただ、最高政府――エル・ゴビエルノ・スプレモ――に、自分が受け取る資格があると信じている年金（月に約一ドル）のことを思い出させてもらうことだけだった。
parts: he asked Charles Gould (whom he took for a mysterious and official person) to do for him
to remind the supreme Government--El Gobierno supreme--of a pension (amounting to about a dollar a month) to which he believed himself entitled
point: 主語 All を修飾する he asked Charles Gould to do for him（ask O to do）や、補語の不定詞の中の believed himself entitled（SVOC）に引っぱられやすい。補語は to remind ~ の不定詞。All was to ~ の第2文型。
explanation: All＝to remind ... の関係。SVC。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: It was evidently a relief to her to be doing something in the way of retrenchment, for, as she said, whenever she paused to think, the recollection of the poor fellow with his bad five-pound note came over her, and she felt quite dishonest; only if it made her so uncomfortable, what must it not be doing to the directors of the bank, who must know so much more of the misery consequent upon this failure?
target: It was evidently a relief to her to be doing something in the way of retrenchment
translation: 節約のために何かをしているのは、明らかに彼女にとって救いだった。というのも、彼女が言うには、立ち止まって考えるたびに、あの不渡りの五ポンド札を持った気の毒な男のことが思い出されて、自分がとても不正直な人間に思えてくるのだった。ただ、それで彼女がこれほど落ち着かないのなら、この破綻から生じる不幸をはるかによく知っているにちがいない銀行の重役たちは、いったいどんな思いをしていることだろう。
parts: to be doing something in the way of retrenchment
point: 真主語の to be doing something が進行形の不定詞で、後半の反語の疑問文や関係詞節も長く、構造を見失いやすい。It は形式主語で、It＝a relief の第2文型。
explanation: It（＝to be doing ...）＝a relief。SVC。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: The General had had nothing to accuse her of, nothing to lay to her charge, but her being the involuntary, unconscious object of a deception which his pride could not pardon, and which a better pride would have been ashamed to own.
translation: 将軍には、彼女を責めるべきことも、彼女のせいにすべきことも何もなかった。あるとすれば、彼女が知らず知らずのうちに、ある思い違いの対象になってしまったということだけだった。それは彼の自尊心が許せない思い違いであり、もっとましな自尊心なら認めるのを恥じたであろう思い違いだった。
parts: nothing to accuse her of, nothing to lay to her charge
but her being the involuntary, unconscious object of a deception which his pride could not pardon, and which a better pride would have been ashamed to own
point: nothing to accuse her of の accuse her（SVO）や but her being ~ に目を奪われやすい。nothing は2つ並ぶが、どちらも had の目的語で、不定詞はそれを修飾する。目的語の並列なので第4文型ではない。第3文型。
explanation: had had は have「持っている」の過去完了。目的語は nothing（to 以下が修飾）。SVO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: ノーサンガー・アビー

text: But from fifteen to seventeen she was in training for a heroine; she read all such works as heroines must read to supply their memories with those quotations which are so serviceable and so soothing in the vicissitudes of their eventful lives.
target: she read all such works as heroines must read to supply their memories with those quotations which are so serviceable and so soothing in the vicissitudes of their eventful lives
translation: しかし十五歳から十七歳まで、彼女はヒロインになるための修業中だった。ヒロインが波乱に富んだ人生の浮き沈みの中でとても役に立ち、心を慰めてくれる引用句を記憶にたくわえるために読まねばならない作品を、彼女はすべて読んだ。
parts: to supply their memories with those quotations which are so serviceable and so soothing in the vicissitudes of their eventful lives
point: such 〜 as の as は関係代名詞で read の目的語なので、as heroines must read を判定しやすい。to supply ~ も目的の不定詞。主節は she read all such works で、目的語1つの第3文型。
explanation: read は他動詞で all such works が目的語。SVO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: ノーサンガー・アビー

text: Her suspense was of full five minutes’ duration; and she was beginning to think it a very long quarter of an hour, when they both returned, and an explanation was given, by Henry’s requesting to know, if she thought her friend, Miss Thorpe, would have any objection to dancing, as his brother would be most happy to be introduced to her.
target: she was beginning to think it a very long quarter of an hour
translation: 彼女のじれったい気持ちはまる五分続いた。そして十五分とはずいぶん長いものだと思いはじめたころ、二人が戻ってきて説明がなされた。ヘンリーが、あなたのお友達のミス・ソープは踊ることに何か差しつかえがあるでしょうか、兄がぜひ紹介していただきたいと言っているのです、と尋ねたのである。
parts: to think it a very long quarter of an hour
point: 不定詞の中の think it a very long quarter of an hour（SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これは目的語の不定詞の中身。begin の目的語は to think ~ の不定詞全体。第3文型。
explanation: begin は他動詞で、to think 以下が目的語。SVO。
note: 不定詞の中の think it a very long quarter of an hour は SVOC だが、文型は主節の動詞 was beginning で判定する。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: ノーサンガー・アビー

text: John Thorpe, in the meanwhile, had walked away; and Catherine, ever willing to give Mr. Tilney an opportunity of repeating the agreeable request which had already flattered her once, made her way to Mrs. Allen and Mrs. Thorpe as fast as she could, in the hope of finding him still with them—a hope which, when it proved to be fruitless, she felt to have been highly unreasonable.
target: Catherine, ever willing to give Mr. Tilney an opportunity of repeating the agreeable request which had already flattered her once, made her way to Mrs. Allen and Mrs. Thorpe as fast as she could, in the hope of finding him still with them
translation: その間にジョン・ソープは立ち去っていた。そして、すでに一度彼女をうれしがらせたあの心地よい申し込みをティルニー氏がもう一度できるよう、いつでもその機会を与えたいと思っていたキャサリンは、彼がまだ二人と一緒にいることを願って、できるだけ急いでアレン夫人とソープ夫人のところへ向かった。その望みは、むなしいとわかってみると、ひどく無理なものだったと彼女は感じた。
parts: ever willing to give Mr. Tilney an opportunity of repeating the agreeable request which had already flattered her once
to Mrs. Allen and Mrs. Thorpe
in the hope of finding him still with them
point: 主語を説明する ever willing to give Mr. Tilney an opportunity（give O1 O2）が目立つので第4文型を選びやすい。in the hope of finding him（find O C）も修飾語。Catherine made her way（進んだ）で第3文型。
explanation: make one’s way「進む」。made が他動詞で her way が目的語。SVO。
note: make one’s way to 〜 を「〜へ向かう」というひとまとまりの表現とみる説明もあるが、形の上では her way が made の目的語。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: ノーサンガー・アビー

text: It gave Lucy the sensation of a fog, and when she reached her own room she opened the window and breathed the clean night air, thinking of the kind old man who had enabled her to see the lights dancing in the Arno and the cypresses of San Miniato, and the foot-hills of the Apennines, black against the rising moon.
target: when she reached her own room she opened the window and breathed the clean night air, thinking of the kind old man who had enabled her to see the lights dancing in the Arno and the cypresses of San Miniato, and the foot-hills of the Apennines, black against the rising moon
translation: それはルーシーに霧の中にいるような感覚を与えた。自分の部屋に戻ると、彼女は窓を開けて夜の澄んだ空気を吸いこみ、アルノ川に踊る灯や、サン・ミニアートの糸杉や、昇る月を背に黒く浮かぶアペニン山脈の麓の丘々を見せてくれたあの親切な老人のことを思った。
parts: when she reached her own room
thinking of the kind old man who had enabled her to see the lights dancing in the Arno and the cypresses of San Miniato, and the foot-hills of the Apennines, black against the rising moon
point: 関係詞節の who had enabled her to see the lights dancing（SVOC の入れ子）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。thinking of ~ も分詞構文。主節は opened the window / breathed the air で第3文型。
explanation: opened the window と breathed the clean night air の2つの SVO が and で並ぶ。SVO。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: On another day, when the whole world was singing and the air ran into the mouth, like wine, she would refuse to stir from the drawing-room, saying that she was an old thing, and no fit companion for a hearty girl.
translation: また別の日には、世界中が歌い、空気がワインのように口に流れこんでくるようなときでも、彼女は応接間から一歩も出ようとせず、自分はもう年寄りで、元気な娘さんの連れには向かない、などと言うのだった。
parts: when the whole world was singing and the air ran into the mouth, like wine
saying that she was an old thing, and no fit companion for a hearty girl
point: saying that ~ の分詞構文や when 節の was singing ~ に引っぱられやすい。また refuse to do の不定詞を補語と見る誤りもある。refuse の目的語は to stir ~ の不定詞。第3文型。
explanation: refuse は他動詞で、to stir 以下が目的語。SVO。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: So now he had asked her once more, and, clear and gentle as ever, she had accepted him, giving no coy reasons for her delay, but simply saying that she loved him and would do her best to make him happy.
target: clear and gentle as ever, she had accepted him, giving no coy reasons for her delay, but simply saying that she loved him and would do her best to make him happy
translation: そこで彼はもう一度申し込み、彼女はいつもどおり澄んだやさしい態度で承諾した。返事を遅らせたことにもったいぶった理由など何も言わず、ただ彼を愛しているし、彼を幸せにするために最善を尽くすつもりだと言っただけだった。
parts: giving no coy reasons for her delay, but simply saying that she loved him and would do her best to make him happy
point: simply saying that ~ の that 節の中の make him happy（SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。clear and gentle as ever も主語の様子を表す修飾語。she had accepted him で第3文型。
explanation: accept は他動詞で him が目的語。SVO。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: She could hardly thank him for the individual kindness, which brought him that very evening to offer her—for the delicacy which made him understand that he must offer her privately—every convenience for illness that his own wealth or his mother’s foresight had caused them to accumulate in their household, and which, as he learnt from Dr. Donaldson, Mrs. Hale might possibly require.
translation: 彼女は、その個人的な親切にほとんど礼を言うこともできなかった。その親切のおかげで彼はまさにその晩やってきて――しかも人目につかないよう申し出なければならないと彼にわからせた心づかいのおかげで――自分の財産や母親の先見の明によって家に蓄えられていた病人用の品々を何でも使ってほしいと申し出てくれたのだ。ドナルドソン医師から聞いたところでは、ヘイル夫人にはそれが必要になるかもしれなかった。
parts: for the individual kindness, which brought him that very evening to offer her—for the delicacy which made him understand that he must offer her privately—every convenience for illness that his own wealth or his mother’s foresight had caused them to accumulate in their household, and which, as he learnt from Dr. Donaldson, Mrs. Hale might possibly require
point: thank は thank 人 for 物の形なので、for 以下の物を2つ目の目的語と見て第4文型を選びやすい。また関係詞節の which made him understand（SVOC）や cause O to do にもつられる。目的語は him の1つで第3文型。
explanation: thank は他動詞で him が目的語。for 以下は理由の M。SVO。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: Margaret had imagined nothing less than that some of the preferments which her mother had so much desired had befallen her father at last—something that would force him to leave beautiful, beloved Helstone, and perhaps compel him to go and live in some of the stately and silent Closes which Margaret had seen from time to time in Cathedral towns.
translation: マーガレットは、母があれほど望んでいた昇進のどれかがとうとう父に訪れたのだ、としか思っていなかった――美しく愛しいヘルストンを離れなければならず、ひょっとすると、ときおり大聖堂のある町で見かけたような、堂々として静かな聖堂境内のどこかへ移り住まねばならなくなるような何かが。
parts: nothing less than that some of the preferments which her mother had so much desired had befallen her father at last—something that would force him to leave beautiful, beloved Helstone, and perhaps compel him to go and live in some of the stately and silent Closes which Margaret had seen from time to time in Cathedral towns
point: nothing less than that 〜（まさに〜ということ）の that 節の中の force him to leave / compel him to go（SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これらは目的語の中身。had imagined nothing ~ で第3文型。
explanation: imagine は他動詞で、nothing less than that 以下が目的語。SVO。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: Margaret poured out the tea in silence, trying to think of something agreeable to say; but her thoughts made answer something like Daniel O’Rourke, when the man-in-the moon asked him to get off his reaping-hook.
target: Margaret poured out the tea in silence, trying to think of something agreeable to say
translation: マーガレットは黙ってお茶を注ぎながら、何か感じのいい話題はないかと考えていた。けれど頭に浮かぶのは、月の男に草刈り鎌から降りろと言われたときのダニエル・オルークの返事のようなものばかりだった。
parts: trying to think of something agreeable to say
point: pour out は「（気持ちを）ぶちまける」の印象もあり、また trying to think of something agreeable to say（分詞構文）に引っぱられやすい。pour out the tea（お茶を注ぐ）で、目的語1つの第3文型。
explanation: pour out は他動詞で the tea が目的語。SVO。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: It was not everybody who could afford to cry so much about their neighbours who had left them nothing; but Mrs Pullet had married a gentleman farmer, and had leisure and money to carry her crying and everything else to the highest pitch of respectability.
target: Mrs Pullet had married a gentleman farmer, and had leisure and money to carry her crying and everything else to the highest pitch of respectability
translation: 何も遺してくれなかった隣人のためにそれほど泣けるのは、誰にでもできることではなかった。しかしプレット夫人は紳士農場主に嫁いでいたので、泣くこともほかの何もかも、立派さの極みまで高めるだけの暇とお金があった。
parts: to carry her crying and everything else to the highest pitch of respectability
point: 前半の It was not everybody who could afford to cry や who had left them nothing（SVOO）に引っぱられて、第4文型を選びやすい。対象は had married a gentleman farmer と had leisure and money で、目的語1つの第3文型。
explanation: married a gentleman farmer と had leisure and money の2つの SVO が並ぶ。SVO。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: As she trod the staircase, narrow, but carpeted thickly, as she entered the eating-room, where saddles of mutton were being trundled up to expectant clergymen, she had a strong, if erroneous, conviction of her own futility, and wished she had never come out of her backwater, where nothing happened except art and literature, and where no one ever got married or succeeded in remaining engaged.
translation: 狭いが厚い絨毯を敷いた階段を上り、羊の背肉が期待に満ちた聖職者たちのところへ運ばれていく食堂に入ると、彼女は、思い違いかもしれないが、自分は役立たずだという強い確信を抱き、自分の淀みから出てこなければよかったと思った。そこでは芸術と文学以外には何も起こらず、誰も結婚せず、婚約を続けることに成功する者もいないのだった。
parts: As she trod the staircase, narrow, but carpeted thickly
as she entered the eating-room, where saddles of mutton were being trundled up to expectant clergymen
she had never come out of her backwater, where nothing happened except art and literature, and where no one ever got married or succeeded in remaining engaged
point: where 節の were being trundled（進行形の受動態）や succeeded in remaining に気を取られやすい。また wished の後ろの that 省略の節を見落としやすい。had a conviction / wished (that) ~ で、どちらも目的語1つの第3文型。
explanation: had a conviction と wished (that) ... の2つの SVO が並ぶ。SVO。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: When the first meeting was over, when our quiet and composure of other days began gradually to return to us, I saw something in my mother’s face which told me that a secret oppression lay heavy on her heart.
translation: 最初の再会が終わり、以前の穏やかで落ち着いた日々が少しずつ戻ってきはじめると、私は母の顔に、ある秘めた重苦しさが母の心にのしかかっていることを告げる何かを見てとった。
parts: When the first meeting was over, when our quiet and composure of other days began gradually to return to us
which told me that a secret oppression lay heavy on her heart
point: 関係詞節の which told me that ~（SVOO）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。これは something を修飾する部分。I saw something で、目的語1つの第3文型。
explanation: saw は他動詞で something が目的語。SVO。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: My conductor led me upstairs into a passage which took us back to the bedchamber in which I had slept during the past night; and opening the door next to it, begged me to look in.
target: My conductor led me upstairs into a passage which took us back to the bedchamber in which I had slept during the past night
translation: 案内人は私を二階へ連れて行き、前の晩に私が眠った寝室へと戻る廊下に入った。そして隣の部屋の戸を開けると、中をのぞいてみるようにと私に言った。
parts: which took us back to the bedchamber in which I had slept during the past night
point: 関係詞節の which took us back to ~（SVO）や後半の begged me to look in（beg O to do、SVOC）に引っぱられやすい。upstairs into a passage も修飾語。My conductor led me で第3文型。
explanation: lead は他動詞で me が目的語。SVO。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: They were chatting and laughing very pleasantly together; and—as proves to be often the case, at moments when we ought to palpitate with sensibility—Clifford and Hepzibah bade a final farewell to the abode of their forefathers, with hardly more emotion than if they had made it their arrangement to return thither at tea-time.
target: Clifford and Hepzibah bade a final farewell to the abode of their forefathers, with hardly more emotion than if they had made it their arrangement to return thither at tea-time
translation: 二人は楽しそうにおしゃべりし、笑い合っていた。そして――感受性で胸を高鳴らせるべきときによくあることだが――クリフォードとヘプジバーは、まるでお茶の時間にはここへ戻る手はずにでもなっているかのように、ほとんど何の感慨もなく先祖代々の住まいに最後の別れを告げた。
parts: to the abode of their forefathers
with hardly more emotion than if they had made it their arrangement to return thither at tea-time
point: bid は bid 人 farewell（人に別れを告げる、第4文型）の形もあるので、第4文型を選びやすい。ここは bid farewell to 〜 で、to 以下は前置詞句。as if 節の中の make it O C も修飾語の中。第3文型。
explanation: bade は他動詞で a final farewell が目的語、to the abode は M。SVO。
note: bid A farewell の語順なら SVOO になる。この文は bid farewell to A の形なので SVO。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン
work: The House of the Seven Gables

text: Such a man should have nothing to do with sorrow; nothing with strife; nothing with the martyrdom which, in an infinite variety of shapes, awaits those who have the heart, and will, and conscience, to fight a battle with the world.
translation: そんな人は悲しみとは何の関わりも持つべきではない。争いとも、そしてまた、限りなくさまざまな形をとって、世間と戦う心と意志と良心を持つ者たちを待ち受けている殉教とも、無縁であるべきなのだ。
parts: nothing to do with sorrow; nothing with strife; nothing with the martyrdom which, in an infinite variety of shapes, awaits those who have the heart, and will, and conscience, to fight a battle with the world
point: have nothing to do with 〜 の to do を補語と見たり、関係詞節や those who have the heart ~ に気を取られたりしやすい。nothing が目的語で、to do with ~ はそれを修飾する不定詞。第3文型。
explanation: have は他動詞で nothing が目的語（2つ目以降の nothing with ... はその繰り返し）。SVO。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン
work: The House of the Seven Gables

text: All the young men felt the attraction of the fine, well-set-up country girls who had come to town to earn a living, and, in nearly every case, to help the father struggle out of debt, or to make it possible for the younger children of the family to go to school.
translation: 若い男たちはみな、暮らしを立てるために町へ出てきた、立派で体格のいい田舎娘たちに惹かれた。娘たちはほとんどの場合、父親が借金から抜け出すのを助けるため、あるいは家族の幼い弟妹が学校へ行けるようにするために来ていたのだった。
parts: of the fine, well-set-up country girls who had come to town to earn a living, and, in nearly every case, to help the father struggle out of debt, or to make it possible for the younger children of the family to go to school
point: girls を修飾する関係詞節の中の help the father struggle（help O 原形）や make it possible for 〜 to go（形式目的語）が目立ち、第5文型を選びやすい。主節は felt the attraction で第3文型。
explanation: felt は他動詞で the attraction が目的語。SVO。
author: Willa Cather
authorJa: ウィラ・キャザー

text: To see him there, a poor afflicted man, earning money by the sweat of his brow, had at first moved her to tears; but to hear him sing and not at all rebel against an occupation which, however satisfactory to himself, was degrading to her, as an educated lady-wife, wounded her through.
translation: 気の毒な不自由な身の夫が、額に汗して金を稼いでいる姿をそこに見たとき、彼女ははじめ涙を流した。だが、彼が歌を歌い、自分にはどれほど満足でも教育を受けた妻である彼女にとっては屈辱的な仕事に、少しも逆らおうとしないのを聞くと、彼女は深く傷ついた。
parts: a poor afflicted man, earning money by the sweat of his brow
but to hear him sing and not at all rebel against an occupation which, however satisfactory to himself, was degrading to her, as an educated lady-wife
point: 主語が2つとも不定詞で、To see him there や to hear him sing（知覚動詞＋O＋原形、SVOC の形）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これらは主語の中身。moved her / wounded her で第3文型。
explanation: moved her と wounded her、どちらも他動詞＋目的語。SVO。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: Miss Jessie began to tell me some more of the plans which had suggested themselves to her, and insensibly fell into talking of the days that were past and gone, and interested me so much I neither knew nor heeded how time passed.
target: Miss Jessie began to tell me some more of the plans which had suggested themselves to her
translation: ジェシー嬢は、思いついた計画のいくつかをさらに私に話しはじめ、いつのまにか過ぎ去った昔の日々の話になっていった。それがあまりにおもしろかったので、私は時のたつのも知らず、気にもとめなかった。
parts: to tell me some more of the plans which had suggested themselves to her
point: 不定詞の中の tell me some more of the plans（SVOO）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。また plans を修飾する関係詞節も長い。begin の目的語は to tell ~ の不定詞全体。第3文型。
explanation: begin は他動詞で、to tell 以下が目的語。SVO。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: They said nothing, but, glancing at me, traced on the glass with their finger-tips the outline of the cherries and strawberries and crabapples within, trying by a blissful expression of countenance to give me some idea of their deliciousness.
translation: 二人は何も言わず、私のほうをちらりと見て、中にあるサクランボやイチゴや野リンゴの輪郭を指先でガラスの上になぞってみせ、うっとりした表情で、そのおいしさを私に何とか伝えようとした。
parts: the outline of the cherries and strawberries and crabapples within
trying by a blissful expression of countenance to give me some idea of their deliciousness
point: 分詞構文の中の give me some idea（SVOO）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。また traced の目的語 the outline ~ が修飾語の後ろに回っていて見落としやすい。said nothing / traced the outline で第3文型。
explanation: said nothing と traced ... the outline の2つの SVO。SVO。
author: Willa Cather
authorJa: ウィラ・キャザー

text: Her father, instead of giving her an unlimited order on his banker, or even putting an hundred pounds bank-bill into her hands, gave her only ten guineas, and promised her more when she wanted it.
translation: 父は、銀行あての無制限の支払い指図書を渡すでも、百ポンドの銀行券を手に握らせるでもなく、たった十ギニーだけを渡し、必要になったらもっと送ると約束した。
parts: instead of giving her an unlimited order on his banker, or even putting an hundred pounds bank-bill into her hands
and promised her more when she wanted it
point: instead of giving her an unlimited order（SVOO の形）に気を取られやすいが、これは前置詞＋動名詞の修飾語。主節は Her father gave her only ten guineas で、her と ten guineas の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: gave her(O1) only ten guineas(O2)。SVOO。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: ノーサンガー・アビー

text: People told them what to see, when to see it, how to stop the electric trams, how to get rid of the beggars, how much to give for a vellum blotter, how much the place would grow upon them.
translation: 人々は彼らに、何を見るべきか、いつ見るべきか、路面電車の止め方、物乞いの追い払い方、子牛皮の吸い取り紙挟みにいくら払えばいいか、その土地がどれほど好きになっていくか、を教えた。
parts: what to see, when to see it, how to stop the electric trams, how to get rid of the beggars, how much to give for a vellum blotter, how much the place would grow upon them
point: 疑問詞＋to不定詞が並び、最後だけ how much the place would grow upon them という節になっているので、目的語の範囲を見失いやすい。これらはまとめて2つ目の目的語。told them ~ で第4文型。
explanation: told them(O1) what to see ...(O2)。SVOO。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: She handed him his cup of tea with the proud air of an unwilling slave; but her eye caught the moment when he was ready for another cup; and he almost longed to ask her to do for him what he saw her compelled to do for her father, who took her little finger and thumb in his masculine hand, and made them serve as sugar-tongues.
target: She handed him his cup of tea with the proud air of an unwilling slave
translation: 彼女は、意に沿わない奴隷のような誇り高い態度で彼にお茶のカップを手渡した。けれど彼がもう一杯ほしくなった瞬間を彼女の目は見逃さなかった。そして彼は、彼女が父親のためにさせられているのを見たことを、自分にもしてほしいとほとんど頼みたくなった。父親は彼女の小指と親指を男らしい手でつまみ、それを角砂糖ばさみの代わりにさせていたのである。
parts: with the proud air of an unwilling slave
point: 後半の longed to ask her to do for him（ask O to do）や made them serve as sugar-tongues（使役の SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。主節は She handed him his cup of tea で第4文型。
explanation: handed him(O1) his cup of tea(O2)。SVOO。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: She looked at her lover with eyes of undiminished trust, and though she had less confidence in her aunt than in a young man with whom she had exchanged so many tender vows, she gave her no handle for explaining or confessing.
target: though she had less confidence in her aunt than in a young man with whom she had exchanged so many tender vows, she gave her no handle for explaining or confessing
translation: 彼女は少しも変わらない信頼のまなざしで恋人を見つめた。そして、あれほど多くのやさしい誓いを交わした若い男に比べれば叔母への信頼は薄かったものの、叔母に、説明したり打ち明けたりするきっかけを与えはしなかった。
parts: though she had less confidence in her aunt than in a young man with whom she had exchanged so many tender vows
no handle for explaining or confessing
point: though 節の中の had less confidence ~ や with whom she had exchanged ~ に気を取られやすい。また no handle for explaining ~ の for 以下を2つ目の要素と見る誤りもある。gave her no handle で第4文型。
explanation: gave her(O1) no handle(O2)。SVOO。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ
workJa: ワシントン・スクエア

text: Of course his easy domestic situation saved him a good deal of drudgery, and his wife’s affiliation to the “best people” brought him a good many of those patients whose symptoms are, if not more interesting in themselves than those of the lower orders, at least more consistently displayed.
target: his wife’s affiliation to the “best people” brought him a good many of those patients whose symptoms are, if not more interesting in themselves than those of the lower orders, at least more consistently displayed
translation: 申し分のない家庭の事情のおかげで彼は多くの骨折り仕事を免れていたし、妻が「上流の人々」とつながっていたことで、多くの患者が彼のもとにやってきた。その症状は、下層の人々の症状よりそれ自体おもしろいとは言えないまでも、少なくとももっと一貫してはっきりと現れるのだった。
parts: a good many of those patients whose symptoms are, if not more interesting in themselves than those of the lower orders, at least more consistently displayed
point: patients を修飾する whose symptoms are ... displayed や、前半の saved him a good deal of drudgery に気を取られやすい。主語も長い。brought him a good many of those patients で第4文型。
explanation: brought him(O1) a good many of those patients(O2)。無生物主語の SVOO。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ
workJa: ワシントン・スクエア

text: As soon as Brahms had grunted himself out, she gave him her card and said, “That is where we live; if you preferred, you could call for the umbrella after the concert, but I didn’t like to trouble you when it has all been our fault.”
target: As soon as Brahms had grunted himself out, she gave him her card
translation: ブラームスがうなるように曲を終えるとすぐ、彼女は彼に名刺を渡してこう言った。「そこが私たちの住まいです。よろしければ、演奏会のあとで傘を取りにいらしてもかまいません。でも、すっかりこちらのせいなのに、ご面倒をおかけしたくなかったものですから」
parts: As soon as Brahms had grunted himself out
point: 前半の grunted himself out（再帰代名詞を使った表現）や、引用の中の call for the umbrella、like to trouble you に気を取られやすい。she gave him her card で、him と card の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: gave him(O1) her card(O2)。SVOO。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: In that moment, when she called me by my name, when she said, “They have tried to make me forget everything, Walter; but I remember Marian, and I remember YOU”—in that moment, I, who had long since given her my love, gave her my life, and thanked God that it was mine to bestow on her.
target: I, who had long since given her my love, gave her my life
translation: その瞬間、彼女が私の名を呼び、「みんなは私に何もかも忘れさせようとしたの、ウォルター。でもマリアンのことは覚えているわ、それにあなたのことも」と言ったその瞬間に、とうに彼女に愛を捧げていた私は、命を捧げた。そして、それが彼女に捧げることのできる自分のものであることを神に感謝した。
parts: who had long since given her my love
point: 挿入の関係詞節 who had long since given her my love も SVOO なので、どちらを判定するか迷いやすい。また引用の中の make me forget（SVOC）にもつられる。主節は gave her my life で第4文型。
explanation: gave her(O1) my life(O2)。SVOO。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: It was more probable, therefore, that the descendants of a Pyncheon who had emigrated to Virginia, in some past generation, and became a great planter there,—hearing of Hepzibah’s destitution, and impelled by the splendid generosity of character with which their Virginian mixture must have enriched the New England blood,—would send her a remittance of a thousand dollars, with a hint of repeating the favor annually.
target: the descendants of a Pyncheon who had emigrated to Virginia, in some past generation, and became a great planter there,—hearing of Hepzibah’s destitution, and impelled by the splendid generosity of character with which their Virginian mixture must have enriched the New England blood,—would send her a remittance of a thousand dollars, with a hint of repeating the favor annually
translation: それよりありそうなのは、何代か前にヴァージニアへ移住して大農園主になったピンチョン家の子孫たちが、ヘプジバーの窮状を耳にし、ヴァージニアの血が混じってニューイングランドの血を豊かにしたにちがいない気前のいい気質に突き動かされて、彼女に千ドルの送金をし、毎年それを繰り返すことをほのめかしてくる、ということだった。
parts: of a Pyncheon who had emigrated to Virginia, in some past generation, and became a great planter there
hearing of Hepzibah’s destitution, and impelled by the splendid generosity of character with which their Virginian mixture must have enriched the New England blood
a remittance of a thousand dollars
with a hint of repeating the favor annually
point: 主語 the descendants の後ろに who 節、分詞構文 hearing of 〜、impelled by 〜 と長く続き、動詞 would send が遠い。with which ~ も修飾語。would send her a remittance で第4文型。
explanation: send her(O1) a remittance(O2)。SVOO。
note: 文全体の主節は It was more probable that ...（形式主語の SVC）。ここでは that 節の中を判定する。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン
work: The House of the Seven Gables

text: At last, in true Costaguana fashion, the Fiscal of Tonoro, who was ambitious of the glory of having reduced the famous Hernandez, offered him a sum of money and a safe conduct out of the country for the betrayal of his band.
translation: とうとう、いかにもコスタグアナらしいやり方で、あの名高いエルナンデスを屈服させたという栄誉を望んでいたトノロの検事が、一味を裏切ることと引き換えに、彼に大金と国外への安全通行証を差し出した。
parts: At last, in true Costaguana fashion
who was ambitious of the glory of having reduced the famous Hernandez
a sum of money and a safe conduct out of the country
for the betrayal of his band
point: 主語の後ろの who was ambitious of the glory of having reduced ~（前置詞＋完了動名詞）に気を取られやすい。offered him a sum of money and a safe conduct で、him と物の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: offered him(O1) a sum of money and a safe conduct(O2)。SVOO。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: But one of my Cargadores, who had been a soldier, told me that he had once ordered a man to be flayed alive in the remote Campo, where he was sent recruiting amongst the people of the Estancias.
translation: しかし、元兵士だった私の荷役人夫の一人が話してくれたところでは、彼はかつて、遠く離れたカンポで男を一人生きたまま皮をはがせたことがあるという。彼はエスタンシアの住民のあいだで兵を募るためにそこへ送られていたのだ。
parts: that he had once ordered a man to be flayed alive in the remote Campo, where he was sent recruiting amongst the people of the Estancias
point: O2 の that 節の中の ordered a man to be flayed alive（order O to do）が第5文型の形なので、そちらを判定しやすい。これは目的語の中身。told me that ~ で第4文型。
explanation: told me(O1) that ...(O2)。SVOO。
author: Joseph Conrad
authorJa: ジョゼフ・コンラッド

text: All the dwellers in Starkfield, as in more notable communities, had had troubles enough of their own to make them comparatively indifferent to those of their neighbours; and though all conceded that Ethan Frome’s had been beyond the common measure, no one gave me an explanation of the look in his face which, as I persisted in thinking, neither poverty nor physical suffering could have put there.
target: no one gave me an explanation of the look in his face which, as I persisted in thinking, neither poverty nor physical suffering could have put there
translation: スタークフィールドの住民はみな、もっと名のある土地の人々と同じく、自分の苦労を十分に抱えていたので、隣人の苦労には比較的無関心だった。そして、イーサン・フロームの苦労が並大抵ではなかったことは誰もが認めていたものの、彼の顔のあの表情について説明してくれる人は一人もいなかった。私はなおも、あれは貧しさや肉体の苦しみが刻みつけたものではありえないと考えていたのだが。
parts: an explanation of the look in his face which, as I persisted in thinking, neither poverty nor physical suffering could have put there
point: 前半の enough to make them comparatively indifferent（make O C）や、the look を修飾する関係詞節に気を取られやすい。no one gave me an explanation で、me と explanation の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: gave me(O1) an explanation ...(O2)。SVOO。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: The “smash-up” it was—I gathered from the same informant—which, besides drawing the red gash across Ethan Frome’s forehead, had so shortened and warped his right side that it cost him a visible effort to take the few steps from his buggy to the post-office window.
target: it cost him a visible effort to take the few steps from his buggy to the post-office window
translation: 私が同じ情報源から聞き集めたところでは、それはあの「激突事故」だった。その事故が、イーサン・フロームの額に赤い傷を刻んだうえ、右半身をすっかり縮めゆがめてしまったので、馬車から郵便局の窓口までのわずかな歩数を進むのにも、彼は目に見えて骨を折らねばならなかった。
parts: to take the few steps from his buggy to the post-office window
point: cost は過去形も cost で動詞と気づきにくく、it を本当の主語と見ると構造を見失いやすい。it は形式主語で、真主語は to take ~。cost him a visible effort で、him と effort の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: cost him(O1) a visible effort(O2)。SVOO。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: He still took refuge there in summer, but when Mattie came to live at the farm he had to give her his stove, and consequently the room was uninhabitable for several months of the year.
target: when Mattie came to live at the farm he had to give her his stove
translation: 夏になると彼は今でもそこに逃げこんでいたが、マッティが農場に住むようになると、ストーブを彼女に譲らなければならず、そのためその部屋は一年のうち数か月は住めなくなった。
parts: when Mattie came to live at the farm
point: had to give の have to を「持つ」と読んで her を目的語と見たり、when 節の came to live に気を取られたりしやすい。have to do は「〜しなければならない」。give her his stove で第4文型。
explanation: have to は助動詞と同じ働きで、V は had to give。give her(O1) his stove(O2)。SVOO。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: Fuchs told me that the sunflowers were introduced into that country by the Mormons; that at the time of the persecution, when they left Missouri and struck out into the wilderness to find a place where they could worship God in their own way, the members of the first exploring party, crossing the plains to Utah, scattered sunflower seed as they went.
translation: フュークスの話では、ヒマワリはモルモン教徒がこの地方に持ちこんだのだという。迫害を受けた時代、彼らはミズーリを離れ、自分たちのやり方で神をあがめられる場所を見つけようと荒野へ乗り出した。そのとき、平原を越えてユタへ向かった最初の探検隊の一行が、進みながらヒマワリの種をまいていったのだ。
parts: that the sunflowers were introduced into that country by the Mormons; that at the time of the persecution, when they left Missouri and struck out into the wilderness to find a place where they could worship God in their own way, the members of the first exploring party, crossing the plains to Utah, scattered sunflower seed as they went
point: O2 の that 節の中の were introduced（受動態）や where they could worship God に気を取られやすい。また that 節が2つあるので目的語の数を見誤る。told me that ~ ; that ~ で第4文型。
explanation: told me(O1) that ...(O2)。SVOO。
author: Willa Cather
authorJa: ウィラ・キャザー

text: If I happened to walk home with her, she told me all about the dresses she was helping to make, or about what she saw and heard when she was with Tiny Soderball at the hotel on Saturday nights.
translation: 私がたまたま彼女と一緒に歩いて帰ると、彼女は手伝って作っているドレスのことや、土曜の夜にホテルでタイニー・ソダーボールと一緒にいたときに見聞きしたことを、何でも話してくれた。
parts: If I happened to walk home with her
all about the dresses she was helping to make, or about what she saw and heard when she was with Tiny Soderball at the hotel on Saturday nights
point: happened to walk の部分や、the dresses (that) she was helping to make（関係代名詞の省略）を判定しやすい。told me all about the dresses で、me と all の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: told me(O1) all about ...(O2)。SVOO。
note: all about 〜 を「〜のすべて」という名詞のまとまりとみて O2 とする。about 以下を修飾語とみて SVO（O＝all）と考える説明もある。
author: Willa Cather
authorJa: ウィラ・キャザー

text: But at length he seemed to find out that she would not be married till she had a “trousseau” to her mind; and then he sent her a letter, which had evidently accompanied a whole box full of finery, and in which he requested that she might be dressed in everything her heart desired.
target: then he sent her a letter, which had evidently accompanied a whole box full of finery, and in which he requested that she might be dressed in everything her heart desired
translation: しかしとうとう彼も、気に入った嫁入り支度がそろうまでは彼女が結婚しないつもりだとわかったようだった。そこで彼は彼女に手紙を送ってきた。その手紙は明らかに、きらびやかな衣装がいっぱい詰まった箱に添えられていたもので、その中で彼は、彼女が心から望むものすべてで着飾ってほしいと頼んでいた。
parts: which had evidently accompanied a whole box full of finery, and in which he requested that she might be dressed in everything her heart desired
point: a letter を修飾する in which he requested that ~ や、前半の seemed to find out に気を取られやすい。sent her a letter で、her と a letter の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: sent her(O1) a letter(O2)。SVOO。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: A low cushion gave him a seat, on which he had disposed himself in the cross-legged attitude of the Bodhisat emerging from meditation; a black teak-wood table, not twenty inches high, set with copper tea-cups, was before him.
target: A low cushion gave him a seat, on which he had disposed himself in the cross-legged attitude of the Bodhisat emerging from meditation
translation: 低いクッションが彼の座になっていて、彼はその上に、瞑想から出てくる菩薩の姿勢で足を組んで座っていた。高さ二十インチもない黒いチークの卓には銅の茶碗が並び、彼の前に置かれていた。
parts: on which he had disposed himself in the cross-legged attitude of the Bodhisat emerging from meditation
point: 主語が無生物の A low cushion で「クッションが彼に席を与えた」と読みにくい。また on which he had disposed himself ~ も紛らわしい。gave him a seat で、him と seat の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: gave him(O1) a seat(O2)。無生物主語の SVOO。
author: Rudyard Kipling
authorJa: ラドヤード・キプリング

text: She did not volunteer the reason which he seemed to hope for, and he wished her good night, going thence round to the back of the house, where he walked up and down by himself for some time before re-entering.
target: he wished her good night, going thence round to the back of the house, where he walked up and down by himself for some time before re-entering
translation: 彼女は、彼が期待しているらしい理由を自分から言おうとはしなかった。彼はおやすみを言うと、そこから家の裏手へ回り、中へ戻る前にしばらく一人で行ったり来たりしていた。
parts: going thence round to the back of the house, where he walked up and down by himself for some time before re-entering
point: wish は「望む」の印象が強く、her good night を「彼女が〜であることを望む」と読み違えて第5文型を選びやすい。wish 人 good night は「人におやすみを言う」で、目的語2つの第4文型。
explanation: wished her(O1) good night(O2)。SVOO。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: He paid them the compliment of crawling between a couple, and, running and halting, crouching and dropping flat, worked his way toward the lighted Mess-tent where, close pressed behind the mango-tree, he waited till some chance word should give him a returnable lead.
target: He paid them the compliment of crawling between a couple
translation: 彼は歩哨たちに敬意を表して、そのうちの二人のあいだを這って抜け、走っては止まり、うずくまっては身を伏せながら、明かりのついた将校食堂のテントのほうへ進んでいった。そしてマンゴーの木の陰にぴったり身を寄せ、誰かのふとした一言が、こちらから返せる手がかりを与えてくれるのを待った。
parts: the compliment of crawling between a couple
point: pay は「払う」の印象が強く、the compliment of crawling ~ の crawling や、後半の分詞構文、till 節の give him a returnable lead に気を取られやすい。paid them the compliment で第4文型。
explanation: paid them(O1) the compliment ...(O2)。SVOO。
author: Rudyard Kipling
authorJa: ラドヤード・キプリング

text: The light air about me told me that the world ended here: only the ground and sun and sky were left, and if one went a little farther there would be only sun and sky, and one would float off into them, like the tawny hawks which sailed over our heads making slow shadows on the grass.
target: The light air about me told me that the world ended here
translation: あたりの軽やかな空気が、世界はここで終わるのだと私に告げていた。残っているのは大地と太陽と空だけで、もう少し先へ行けば太陽と空しかなくなり、私たちの頭上を舞って草の上にゆっくりと影を落としていく黄褐色の鷹のように、その中へ漂い出ていってしまうだろう。
point: 主語が無生物の The light air で「空気が私に告げた」と読みにくい。後半の which sailed over our heads や仮定法にも気を取られる。told me that the world ended here で第4文型。
explanation: told me(O1) that ...(O2)。無生物主語の SVOO。
author: Willa Cather
authorJa: ウィラ・キャザー

text: That she might not appear, however, to observe or expect him, she kept her eyes intently fixed on her fan; and a self-condemnation for her folly, in supposing that among such a crowd they should even meet with the Tilneys in any reasonable time, had just passed through her mind, when she suddenly found herself addressed and again solicited to dance, by Mr. Tilney himself.
target: That she might not appear, however, to observe or expect him, she kept her eyes intently fixed on her fan
translation: けれども、彼を見ているとも待っているとも思われないように、彼女は目をじっと扇に注いでいた。そして、あれほどの人ごみの中でほどよい時間のうちにティルニー兄妹に会えるなどと思った自分の愚かさを責める気持ちがちょうど胸をよぎったとき、不意に声をかけられ、もう一度ダンスを申しこまれた。ティルニー氏本人からだった。
parts: That she might not appear, however, to observe or expect him
point: 文頭の That she might not appear ~（目的を表す節）や、後半の found herself addressed ~（SVOC）に気を取られやすい。対象は kept her eyes intently fixed で、eyes＝fixed の第5文型。
explanation: keep O C「O を C の状態に保つ」。her eyes＝fixed の関係。SVOC。
author: Jane Austen
authorJa: ジェイン・オースティン
workJa: ノーサンガー・アビー

text: He left them, carefully closing the front door; and when they looked through the hall window, they saw him go up the drive and begin to climb the slopes of withered fern behind the house.
target: when they looked through the hall window, they saw him go up the drive and begin to climb the slopes of withered fern behind the house
translation: 彼は玄関の戸を注意深く閉めて二人のもとを去った。玄関ホールの窓からのぞくと、彼が車寄せの道を上っていき、家の裏手の枯れたシダの斜面を登りはじめるのが見えた。
parts: when they looked through the hall window
go up the drive and begin to climb the slopes of withered fern behind the house
point: begin to climb の不定詞を目的語と見て第3文型を選びやすい。また closing the front door の分詞構文にもつられる。知覚動詞 see＋O＋原形で、him が go up / begin する関係。第5文型。
explanation: see O C「O が C するのを見る」。him＝go up ... and begin ... の関係。SVOC。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: The little cherub Laura, not being an accomplished walker at present, had a ribbon fastened round her waist, by which Tom held her as if she had been a little dog during the minutes in which she chose to walk; but as these were rare, he was for the most part carrying this fine child round and round the garden, within sight of Mrs Stelling’s window, according to orders.
target: The little cherub Laura, not being an accomplished walker at present, had a ribbon fastened round her waist, by which Tom held her as if she had been a little dog during the minutes in which she chose to walk
translation: 小さな天使のようなローラは、今のところまだ歩くのが上手ではなかったので、腰にリボンを結びつけられていた。そして彼女が歩く気になった数分のあいだは、トムがまるで子犬でも連れているかのようにそのリボンでつかまえていた。
parts: not being an accomplished walker at present
by which Tom held her as if she had been a little dog during the minutes in which she chose to walk
point: not being an accomplished walker（分詞構文）や by which Tom held her、in which she chose to walk に気を取られやすい。have O＋過去分詞で、ribbon＝fastened の関係。第5文型。
explanation: have O＋過去分詞「O を〜してもらう／〜された状態にある」。a ribbon＝fastened の関係。SVOC。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: But the absence of that cloud only left it more apparent that the cloud of severity remained; and Mr Glegg, perceiving this, as he sat down to his milkporridge, which it was his old frugal habit to stem his morning hunger with, prudently resolved to leave the first remark to Mrs Glegg, lest, to so delicate an article as a lady’s temper, the slightest touch should do mischief.
target: the absence of that cloud only left it more apparent that the cloud of severity remained
translation: しかしその雲がないことで、かえって厳しさの雲が残っていることがいっそうはっきりしただけだった。グレッグ氏はそれに気づくと、朝の空腹をそれでしのぐのが昔からの倹約の習慣である牛乳がゆの前に座りながら、最初のひと言はグレッグ夫人に任せようと賢明にも心に決めた。ご婦人の機嫌のようなこれほど繊細な代物には、ほんのわずかに触れただけでも害になりかねないからである。
parts: that the cloud of severity remained
point: it を本当の目的語と思うと、that 節の扱いに困って第3文型などを選びやすい。また後半の perceiving this や resolved to leave にもつられる。it は形式目的語で、真の目的語は that 節。it＝more apparent の第5文型。
explanation: leave it more apparent that ...「〜をいっそう明らかな状態にする」。O(仮)＝C の関係。SVOC。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: If we only look far enough off for the consequence of our actions, we can always find some point in the combination of results by which those actions can be justified; by adopting the point of view of a Providence who arranges results, or of a philosopher who traces them, we shall find it possible to obtain perfect complacency in choosing to do what is most agreeable to us in the present moment.
target: by adopting the point of view of a Providence who arranges results, or of a philosopher who traces them, we shall find it possible to obtain perfect complacency in choosing to do what is most agreeable to us in the present moment
translation: 自分の行いの結果をはるか遠くまで見ていきさえすれば、いつでも結果の組み合わせの中に、その行いを正当化できる点を何か見つけられるものだ。結果を按配する神の摂理の立場や、結果をたどる哲学者の立場をとることで、私たちはいまこの瞬間にいちばん心地よいことをするのを選びながら、完全に満ち足りた気持ちでいることができると気づくのである。
parts: by adopting the point of view of a Providence who arranges results, or of a philosopher who traces them
to obtain perfect complacency in choosing to do what is most agreeable to us in the present moment
point: 文頭の by adopting the point of view ~ や who arranges results などの関係詞節が長く、動詞を見失いやすい。また it を本当の目的語と見る誤りもある。it は形式目的語で、真の目的語は to obtain ~。it＝possible の第5文型。
explanation: find it possible to do「〜できるとわかる」。SVOC。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: The young man, within a few days, had made her listen to things for which she had not supposed that she was prepared; having a lively foreboding of difficulties, he proceeded to gain as much ground as possible in the present.
target: The young man, within a few days, had made her listen to things for which she had not supposed that she was prepared
translation: その若い男は数日のうちに、彼女が心の準備ができているとは思ってもみなかったような話に耳を傾けさせていた。行く手の困難を強く予感していたので、彼は今のうちにできるだけ地歩を固めようとしたのである。
parts: listen to things for which she had not supposed that she was prepared
point: listen を動詞の原形と気づかず、her を目的語と見て第3文型を選びやすい。また proceeded to gain ~ にもつられる。使役の make＋O＋原形で、her が listen する関係。第5文型。
explanation: make O C「O に C させる」。her＝listen の関係。SVOC。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ
workJa: ワシントン・スクエア

text: Driving out to Bloomingdale one April day to see a patient of unsound mind, who was confined in a private asylum for the insane, and whose family greatly desired a medical opinion from an eminent source, he was caught in a spring shower, and being in a buggy, without a hood, he found himself soaked to the skin.
target: being in a buggy, without a hood, he found himself soaked to the skin
translation: ある四月の日、私立の精神病院に収容されている心を病んだ患者を診に、ブルーミングデールまで馬車で出かけた――その家族は名高い医師の診断をぜひにと望んでいたのだ――彼は春のにわか雨に降られ、幌のない軽馬車だったので、気がつくと肌までずぶ濡れになっていた。
parts: being in a buggy, without a hood
point: 文頭の Driving out ~ や being in a buggy の分詞構文、patient を修飾する関係詞節に気を取られ、動詞を見失いやすい。find oneself＋過去分詞（気づくと〜されていた）で、himself＝soaked。第5文型。
explanation: find oneself C「気がつくと C の状態だ」。himself＝soaked の関係。SVOC。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ
workJa: ワシントン・スクエア

text: The remark would be untrue, but of the kind which, if stated often enough, may become true; just as the remark, “England and Germany are bound to fight,” renders war a little more likely each time that it is made, and is therefore made the more readily by the gutter press of either nation.
target: the remark, “England and Germany are bound to fight,” renders war a little more likely each time that it is made
translation: その言葉は真実ではないだろうが、何度も口にされると真実になりかねない類のものだった。ちょうど「イギリスとドイツは戦う運命にある」という言葉が、口にされるたびに戦争を少しずつ起こりやすくし、それゆえ両国の低俗な新聞によってますます気軽に口にされるのと同じように。
parts: “England and Germany are bound to fight,”
each time that it is made
point: 引用の England and Germany are bound to fight（be bound to do）や、the kind which ... may become true（SVC）に引っぱられて第2文型を選びやすい。render O C（O を C にする）で、war＝more likely。第5文型。
explanation: render O C「O を C にする」。war＝a little more likely の関係。SVOC。
author: E. M. Forster
authorJa: E・M・フォースター

text: Events which I have yet to relate make it necessary to mention in this place that my father had been dead some years at the period of which I am now writing; and that my sister Sarah and I were the sole survivors of a family of five children.
translation: これから語らなければならない出来事のために、ここで次のことを述べておく必要がある。いま書いている当時、父は亡くなって数年がたっていた。そして妹のセアラと私が、五人きょうだいのうちのただ二人の生き残りだった。
parts: which I have yet to relate
to mention in this place that my father had been dead some years at the period of which I am now writing; and that my sister Sarah and I were the sole survivors of a family of five children
point: it を本当の目的語と思うと、to mention ~ の扱いに困って第3文型を選びやすい。また which I have yet to relate も紛らわしい。it は形式目的語で、真の目的語は to mention ~。it＝necessary の第5文型。
explanation: make it necessary to do「〜することを必要にする」。SVOC。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: Velvet garments sombre but rich, stiffly plaited ruffs and bands, embroidered gloves, venerable beards, the mien and countenance of authority, made it easy to distinguish the gentleman of worship, at that period, from the tradesman, with his plodding air, or the laborer, in his leathern jerkin, stealing awe-stricken into the house which he had perhaps helped to build.
translation: 地味だが豪華なビロードの衣服、固くひだを取った襞襟や垂れ襟、刺繍入りの手袋、威厳ある顎ひげ、権威を帯びた物腰と顔つき――そうしたものによって、当時は身分ある紳士を、とぼとぼした様子の商人や、革の上着を着て、ひょっとすると自分も建てるのを手伝ったかもしれないその家へおそるおそる忍びこむ労働者と、たやすく見分けることができた。
parts: Velvet garments sombre but rich, stiffly plaited ruffs and bands, embroidered gloves, venerable beards, the mien and countenance of authority

to distinguish the gentleman of worship, at that period, from the tradesman, with his plodding air, or the laborer, in his leathern jerkin, stealing awe-stricken into the house which he had perhaps helped to build
point: 主語が名詞を並べた長い句で、plaited / embroidered などの過去分詞を動詞と見誤りやすい。また it を本当の目的語と見る誤りもある。it は形式目的語で、真の目的語は to distinguish ~。it＝easy の第5文型。
explanation: make it easy to do「〜することを容易にする」。SVOC。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン
work: The House of the Seven Gables

text: But, as it happened, scarcely had Phœbe’s eyes rested again on the Judge’s countenance than all its ugly sternness vanished; and she found herself quite overpowered by the sultry, dog-day heat, as it were, of benevolence, which this excellent man diffused out of his great heart into the surrounding atmosphere,—very much like a serpent, which, as a preliminary to fascination, is said to fill the air with his peculiar odor.
target: she found herself quite overpowered by the sultry, dog-day heat, as it were, of benevolence, which this excellent man diffused out of his great heart into the surrounding atmosphere
translation: ところが、フィービーの目が判事の顔にふたたびとまるやいなや、その醜い厳しさはすっかり消えてしまった。そして彼女は、この立派な人物が大きな心から周囲の空気へと発散させる、いわば土用の蒸し暑さのような善意にすっかり圧倒されてしまった。魅了する前触れとして独特のにおいで空気を満たすと言われる蛇によく似ていた。
parts: by the sultry, dog-day heat, as it were, of benevolence, which this excellent man diffused out of his great heart into the surrounding atmosphere
point: overpowered を受動態の動詞と見て、第3文型を選びやすい。また後半の scarcely had 〜 than ... の倒置や関係詞節にもつられる。find oneself＋過去分詞で、herself＝overpowered。第5文型。
explanation: find oneself＋過去分詞「気がつくと〜されている」。herself＝overpowered の関係。SVOC。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン
work: The House of the Seven Gables

text: Could the Judge but quaff a glass, it might enable him to shake off the unaccountable lethargy which (for the ten intervening minutes, and five to boot, are already past) has made him such a laggard at this momentous dinner.
target: it might enable him to shake off the unaccountable lethargy which (for the ten intervening minutes, and five to boot, are already past) has made him such a laggard at this momentous dinner
translation: 判事がせめて一杯でも飲み干せたなら、それで彼は、この大事な晩餐に彼をこれほど遅れさせているわけのわからない無気力を振り払えるかもしれない（なにしろ間の十分に、おまけの五分も、もう過ぎてしまっているのだ）。
parts: to shake off the unaccountable lethargy which (for the ten intervening minutes, and five to boot, are already past) has made him such a laggard at this momentous dinner
point: to shake off ~ を目的の不定詞と見て、him だけを目的語とする第3文型を選びやすい。また関係詞節の中の has made him such a laggard（SVOC）も紛らわしい。enable O to do で、him が shake off する関係。第5文型。
explanation: enable him to shake off ...。him＝to shake off の関係。SVOC。
note: enable O to do は「O が〜する」という主述関係があるため、このクイズでは SVOC として扱う。
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
authorJa: ナサニエル・ホーソーン
work: The House of the Seven Gables

text: Suddenly it occurred to him that Andrew Hale, who was a kind-hearted man, might be induced to reconsider his refusal and advance a small sum on the lumber if he were told that Zeena’s ill-health made it necessary to hire a servant.
target: Zeena’s ill-health made it necessary to hire a servant
translation: ふと彼は思いついた。アンドルー・ヘイルは心のやさしい男だから、もしジーナの病気のせいで使用人を雇わなければならなくなったと聞かされれば、断ったことを考え直して、材木を担保にわずかな額を前貸ししてくれる気になるかもしれない。
point: it を本当の目的語と見ると、to hire a servant を目的の修飾語と読んで第3文型を選びやすい。it は形式目的語で、真の目的語は to hire a servant。it＝necessary の第5文型。
explanation: make it necessary to do。if 節の that 節の中の文型を判定する。SVOC。
note: 文全体の主節は it occurred to him that ...（形式主語の SV）。ここでは that 節の中の if 節のさらに中を問う。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: After the funeral, when he saw her preparing to go away, he was seized with an unreasoning dread of being left alone on the farm; and before he knew what he was doing he had asked her to stay there with him.
target: he saw her preparing to go away
translation: 葬式のあと、彼女が出ていく支度をしているのを見ると、彼はこの農場に一人取り残されることへの理屈に合わない恐怖にとらわれた。そして自分が何をしているのかわからないうちに、ここに残って一緒にいてほしいと彼女に頼んでいた。
point: preparing to go away を目的語の一部と見たり、prepare to do の不定詞に気を取られたりしやすい。後半の asked her to stay（SVOC）もある。知覚動詞 see＋O＋-ing で、her が preparing する関係。第5文型。
explanation: see O＋-ing「O が〜しているのを見る」。her＝preparing の関係。SVOC。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: At the moment Ethan Frome, after climbing to his seat, had leaned over to assure himself of the security of a wooden box—also with a druggist’s label on it—which he had placed in the back of the buggy, and I saw his face as it probably looked when he thought himself alone.
target: he thought himself alone
translation: そのとき、イーサン・フロームは座席に上ったあと、身を乗り出して、馬車の後ろに置いた木箱――これにも薬屋のラベルが貼ってあった――がしっかりしているか確かめていた。そして私は、自分は一人きりだと思っているときにおそらく見せるであろう彼の顔を見たのだった。
point: think は「〜と思う」で that 節をとる第3文型の印象が強く、alone を修飾語と見て第3文型を選びやすい。think O C（O を C だと思う）で、himself＝alone。第5文型。
explanation: think O C「O を C だと思う」。himself＝alone の関係。SVOC。
author: Edith Wharton
authorJa: イーディス・ウォートン

text: I was getting the parlour fire lighted, and one of the servants was preparing tea, for I wanted them to have something to eat and drink and warm them, when old Clare asked to speak to me.
target: I wanted them to have something to eat and drink and warm them
translation: 私が客間の暖炉に火を入れさせ、使用人の一人がお茶の支度をしていた。みんなに何か食べたり飲んだりして体を温めるものをとってほしかったからだ。そのとき、クレアじいさんが私に話があると言ってきた。
parts: to have something to eat and drink and warm them
point: something to eat and drink and warm them の warm them（SVO）や、前半の getting the parlour fire lighted に気を取られやすい。want O to do で、them が have する関係。第5文型。
explanation: want them to have ...。them＝to have の関係。SVOC。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: When we came back, nothing would serve him but he must read us the poems he had been speaking of; and Miss Pole encouraged him in his proposal, I thought, because she wished me to hear his beautiful reading, of which she had boasted; but she afterwards said it was because she had got to a difficult part of her crochet, and wanted to count her stitches without having to talk.
target: she wished me to hear his beautiful reading, of which she had boasted
translation: 私たちが戻ると、彼は話していた詩を読んで聞かせるのだと言ってききませんでした。ポール嬢がその申し出を後押ししたのは、彼女がかねて自慢していた彼の見事な朗読を私に聞かせたかったからだと私は思いました。けれどあとで彼女が言うには、かぎ針編みのむずかしいところにさしかかったので、話をしないで目を数えたかったからなのでした。
parts: to hear his beautiful reading, of which she had boasted
point: wish は wish 人 物（第4文型）にもなるので、to hear 以下を2つ目の目的語と見やすい。wish O to do（O に〜してほしい）で、me が hear する関係。of which she had boasted も修飾語。第5文型。
explanation: wish me to hear ...。me＝to hear の関係。SVOC。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: At first they breathed temperately upon the travellers, winds good to meet when one crawled over some gigantic hog’s-back; but in a few days, at a height of nine or ten thousand feet, those breezes bit; and Kim kindly allowed a village of hillmen to acquire merit by giving him a rough blanket-coat.
target: Kim kindly allowed a village of hillmen to acquire merit by giving him a rough blanket-coat
translation: はじめのうち風は旅人たちにおだやかに吹きつけ、巨大な豚の背のような尾根を這い越えるときには、出会えばありがたい風だった。だが数日たって九千から一万フィートの高さになると、その風は肌を刺すようになった。そしてキムは寛大にも、ある山の民の村に、自分に粗い毛布の外套をくれることで功徳を積ませてやったのである。
parts: to acquire merit by giving him a rough blanket-coat
point: by giving him a rough blanket-coat（give O1 O2）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。これは前置詞＋動名詞の修飾語。allow O to do で、a village が acquire merit する関係。第5文型。
explanation: allow a village of hillmen to acquire merit。O＝to acquire の関係。SVOC。
author: Rudyard Kipling
authorJa: ラドヤード・キプリング

text: But the concentration upon her part necessary to prevent discovery, the newness of the scene, the shine of the candles, and the confusing effect upon her vision of the ribboned visor which hid her features, left her absolutely unable to perceive who were present as spectators.
translation: けれども、見破られないようにするために彼女に必要だった集中と、場面の目新しさと、ろうそくの輝きと、顔を隠しているリボンのついた面頬が視界を乱すせいとで、彼女は見物人として誰が居合わせているのか、まったく見分けることができなかった。
parts: the concentration upon her part necessary to prevent discovery, the newness of the scene, the shine of the candles, and the confusing effect upon her vision of the ribboned visor which hid her features
absolutely unable to perceive who were present as spectators
point: 主語が4つの名詞句と長く、necessary to prevent discovery や which hid her features に動詞を探して迷いやすい。leave O C（O を C の状態にする）で、her＝unable to perceive ~。第5文型。
explanation: leave O C「O を C の状態にしておく」。her＝unable の関係。SVOC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: When I went upstairs to-day, after lunch, to put on my bonnet for a walk, she volunteered to join me, and again, before dinner, she threw the door open between our two rooms, so that we might talk to each other while we were dressing.
target: she threw the door open between our two rooms, so that we might talk to each other while we were dressing
translation: 今日、昼食のあと散歩に出るためにボンネットをかぶりに二階へ上がると、彼女は一緒に行くと自分から言い出した。そしてまた夕食の前には、着替えながら二人で話ができるように、私たちの二つの部屋のあいだの戸を開け放った。
parts: between our two rooms, so that we might talk to each other while we were dressing
point: open を「開ける」という動詞と見て、throw と open の2つの動詞が並ぶと読みやすい。また to put on my bonnet などの不定詞にもつられる。throw O open（O をさっと開ける）の open は形容詞で、door＝open。第5文型。
explanation: threw the door(O) open(C)。the door＝open の関係。SVOC。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: The young woman his wife, who seemed accustomed to such remarks, acted as if she did not hear them, and continued her intermittent private words of tender trifles to the sleeping and waking child, who was just big enough to be placed for a moment on the bench beside her when she wished to ease her arms.
target: The young woman his wife, who seemed accustomed to such remarks, acted as if she did not hear them
translation: その若い女、つまり彼の妻は、そうした言葉には慣れているらしく、聞こえないかのように振る舞い、眠ったり目を覚ましたりする子どもに、優しいたわいもない言葉を途切れ途切れにささやき続けた。子どもは、彼女が腕を休めたいときに少しのあいだ隣の腰掛けに置いておけるくらいの大きさになっていた。
parts: who seemed accustomed to such remarks
as if she did not hear them
point: 挿入の who seemed accustomed to such remarks（SVC）や、child を修飾する enough to be placed ~ に気を取られやすい。act は「演じる」の他動詞にもなるが、ここは自動詞。The young woman acted で第1文型。
explanation: act は「振る舞う」の自動詞で、as if 以下は様態の副詞節。判定部分は SV（後半 continued her ... words は別の SVO）。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: カスターブリッジの市長

text: There was a dog howling all night under my window, which may have had something to do with it; or it may have been the paprika, for I had to drink up all the water in my carafe, and was still thirsty.
target: There was a dog howling all night under my window
translation: 一晩じゅう窓の下で犬が遠吠えしていて、それが関係していたのかもしれない。あるいはパプリカのせいだったのかもしれない。というのも水差しの水を全部飲み干さねばならず、それでもまだ喉が渇いていたからだ。
parts: howling all night under my window
point: howling all night を進行形の動詞と見たり、a dog を補語と見たりしやすい。また which may have had something to do with it にもつられる。There was＋主語の存在文で、howling 以下は a dog を修飾。第1文型。
explanation: There is 構文の There は M、主語は a dog。be 動詞が「いる」の意味なので SV。
author: Bram Stoker
authorJa: ブラム・ストーカー

text: The rendition ran on in this wise until it came to where Carrie, as Laura, comes into the room to explain to Ray, who, after hearing Pearl’s statement about her birth, had written the letter repudiating her, which, however, he did not deliver.
translation: 上演はこの調子で進み、やがてキャリーがローラとして部屋に入り、レイに説明する場面に来た。レイはパールの出生にまつわる話を聞いたあと、彼女と縁を切る手紙を書いていたが、それを渡してはいなかった。
parts: until it came to where Carrie, as Laura, comes into the room to explain to Ray, who, after hearing Pearl’s statement about her birth, had written the letter repudiating her, which, however, he did not deliver
point: came to where 〜、to explain、who ... had written、which he did not deliver など目的語を含む節が多く、第3文型を選びやすい。run on は「続く」の自動詞。主節は The rendition ran on で第1文型。
explanation: run on は「どんどん進む・続く」の自動詞。in this wise「このようにして」と until 節は M。SV。
author: Theodore Dreiser
authorJa: セオドア・ドライサー

text: He sat next Fancy, and had the thrilling pleasure of using permanently a glass which had been taken by Fancy in mistake; of letting the outer edge of the sole of his boot touch the lower verge of her skirt; and to add to these delights the cat, which had lain unobserved in her lap for several minutes, crept across into his own, touching him with fur that had touched her hand a moment before.
target: the cat, which had lain unobserved in her lap for several minutes, crept across into his own, touching him with fur that had touched her hand a moment before
translation: 彼はファンシーの隣に座り、ファンシーが間違えて取ったグラスをそのまま使い続けるという胸の震えるような喜びを味わい、靴底の外の縁を彼女のスカートの裾に触れさせた。さらにこうした喜びに加えて、何分も前から彼女の膝の上で人知れず寝ていた猫が、彼の膝へと渡ってきて、つい今しがた彼女の手に触れていた毛で彼に触れたのだった。
parts: which had lain unobserved in her lap for several minutes
touching him with fur that had touched her hand a moment before
point: which had lain unobserved（lie の過去分詞）を他動詞 lay と見誤ったり、touching him with fur の him を目的語と見たりしやすい。主節は the cat crept（creep の過去形、自動詞）で第1文型。
explanation: creep「這う・そっと移る」は自動詞。across into his own（=lap）は M。判定部分は SV。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: He was, during the journey, subjected to such a weight of unanswerable argument, all of which went to prove that it was his bounden duty not to interfere with the paternal Government that was so anxious to make him a dean, that when he arrived at the chemist's door in High Street, he hardly knew which way to turn himself in the matter.
translation: 道中ずっと、彼は反論しようのない議論を山ほど浴びせられた。それはどれも、自分を主任司祭にしようと熱心な父親のような政府に口出しをしないのが自分の当然の義務だと証明するものだった。そのため、ハイ・ストリートの薬屋の戸口に着いたときには、この件でどちらに向かえばよいのか、ほとんどわからなくなっていた。
parts: to such a weight of unanswerable argument, all of which went to prove that it was his bounden duty not to interfere with the paternal Government that was so anxious to make him a dean, that when he arrived at the chemist's door in High Street, he hardly knew which way to turn himself in the matter
point: subject は「〜を従わせる」の他動詞で、また後半の make him a dean（SVOC）、which way to turn himself も目立つので、第3文型や第5文型を選びやすい。この文は受動態で、目的語は残らない。第1文型。
explanation: subject O to 〜「O に〜を受けさせる」の受動態で、to 以下は M。受動態で後ろに修飾語しかないので SV。
author: Anthony Trollope
authorJa: アントニー・トロロープ

text: He was looking at the book, the position of which caused him to stand with his back turned towards the closed folding doors communicating with the front room, when, without the slightest previous noise to warn him, he felt himself suddenly seized round the neck from behind.
translation: 彼はその本を眺めていた。本の置き場所のせいで、表の部屋に通じる閉じた折り戸に背を向けて立っていた。そのとき、前触れの物音ひとつなく、彼は不意に背後から首をつかまれるのを感じた。
parts: the position of which caused him to stand with his back turned towards the closed folding doors communicating with the front room
when, without the slightest previous noise to warn him, he felt himself suddenly seized round the neck from behind
point: 関係詞節の caused him to stand（SVOC）や with his back turned（付帯状況）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。look は「見る」の自動詞で、at などの前置詞句は修飾語。He was looking で第1文型。
explanation: look は自動詞、at the book は前置詞句で M。学校文法では SV。
note: look at をひとまとまりの他動詞とみて the book を目的語とする立場では SVO。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: Since, however, Dr. Van Helsing has been with me, all this bad dreaming seems to have passed away; the noises that used to frighten me out of my wits--the flapping against the windows, the distant voices which seemed so close to me, the harsh sounds that came from I know not where and commanded me to do I know not what--have all ceased.
target: the noises that used to frighten me out of my wits--the flapping against the windows, the distant voices which seemed so close to me, the harsh sounds that came from I know not where and commanded me to do I know not what--have all ceased
translation: けれどもヴァン・ヘルシング先生がそばにいてくださるようになってから、悪い夢はすっかり消えたようだ。正気を失うほど私を怖がらせていた物音――窓をはたくはばたき、すぐそばにいるように聞こえる遠い声、どこからともなく聞こえてきて何とも知れぬことをせよと命じる耳ざわりな音――は、すべてやんでしまった。
parts: that used to frighten me out of my wits
the flapping against the windows, the distant voices which seemed so close to me, the harsh sounds that came from I know not where and commanded me to do I know not what
point: 主語の後ろの that used to frighten me out of my wits や commanded me to do ~（SVOC）が長く、そちらを判定しやすい。また主語が言い換えで2つある。cease は「止む」の自動詞。have all ceased で第1文型。
explanation: 主語は the noises（とその言い換え）、動詞は cease「やむ」の自動詞。all は副詞的に主語を受ける。SV。
author: Bram Stoker
authorJa: ブラム・ストーカー

text: But when she left them to disenjoy themselves in their own way Harry Haydock put a one-step record on the phonograph, the younger people took the floor, and all the elders sneaked back to their chairs, with crystallized smiles which meant, “Don't believe I'll try this one myself, but I do enjoy watching the youngsters dance.”
target: all the elders sneaked back to their chairs, with crystallized smiles which meant, “Don't believe I'll try this one myself, but I do enjoy watching the youngsters dance
translation: しかし彼女がその人たちを好きなように退屈させておくことにして離れると、ハリー・ヘイドックが蓄音機にワンステップのレコードをかけ、若い人たちがフロアに出た。年配の者はみな、固まった笑みを浮かべてそっと椅子に戻った。その笑みは「自分でやってみる気はないが、若い者が踊るのを見るのは実に楽しい」という意味だった。
parts: with crystallized smiles which meant, “Don't believe I'll try this one myself, but I do enjoy watching the youngsters dance
point: sneak は「〜をこっそり持ち出す」の他動詞にもなるので目的語を探しやすく、また left them to disenjoy、watching the youngsters dance（SVOC）にもつられる。sneaked back to ~（こっそり戻った）で第1文型。
explanation: sneak「こっそり動く」は自動詞。back to their chairs と with 以下は M。判定部分は SV。
author: Sinclair Lewis
authorJa: シンクレア・ルイス
