text: The glorious past, in which men and women grew to unexampled size, intruded too much upon the present, and dwarfed it too consistently, to be altogether encouraging to one forced to make her experiment in living when the great age was dead.
target: The glorious past, in which men and women grew to unexampled size, intruded too much upon the present
translation: 男も女も比類のない大きさに育った輝かしい過去は、現在にあまりにも割りこみ、あまりにも一貫して現在を小さく見せたので、偉大な時代が終わったあとで生きる試みをせねばならない者にとって、とても励みになるものではなかった。
parts: in which men and women grew to unexampled size
point: intrude は「〜を押しつける」の他動詞にもなるので目的語を探しやすく、また too 〜 to 構文や forced to make にもつられる。挿入の in which 節も長い。The glorious past intruded で第1文型。
explanation: intrude upon 〜「〜に割りこむ」の intrude は自動詞で、upon the present は M。SV。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: Tales are told of the consternation once caused among the church fiddlers when, on the occasion of their producing a new Christmas anthem, he did not come to time, owing to being snowed up on the downs, and the straits they were in through having to make shift with whipcord and twine for strings.
translation: かつて教会の弦楽隊のあいだに起きた大騒ぎの話が語り伝えられている。新しいクリスマスの聖歌を披露するという日に、彼が丘で雪に閉じこめられて時間に間に合わず、弦の代わりに鞭ひもや麻ひもで間に合わせねばならなくなった窮地の話である。
parts: once caused among the church fiddlers

when, on the occasion of their producing a new Christmas anthem, he did not come to time, owing to being snowed up on the downs, and the straits they were in through having to make shift with whipcord and twine for strings
point: tell は第4文型の代表的な動詞なので、第4文型や第3文型を選びやすい。この文は受動態で、Tales ... of the consternation の of 句が動詞の後ろに回っているだけ。目的語は残らない。第1文型。
explanation: tell の受動態で、後ろは修飾語だけ。SV。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: Then there was lunch, when every one was merry and hungry, excepting the hostess, who was trying to train her midday appetite into the genteelest of all ways, and thought (falsely enough) that Dr. Nicholls was a good person to practise the semblance of ill-health upon, and that he would give her the proper civil amount of commiseration for her ailments, which every guest ought to bestow upon a hostess who complains of her delicacy of health.
translation: それから昼食になった。皆が陽気で空腹だったが、女主人だけは別だった。彼女は昼の食欲をいちばん上品な形に慣らそうとしていて、（まったくの見当違いだが）ニコルズ先生は病弱のふりを練習するのにうってつけの相手だ、体の弱さをこぼす女主人に客ならだれでも示すべき、ほどよい礼儀正しい同情を自分の病に寄せてくれるだろう、と考えていた。
parts: when every one was merry and hungry, excepting the hostess, who was trying to train her midday appetite into the genteelest of all ways, and thought (falsely enough) that Dr. Nicholls was a good person to practise the semblance of ill-health upon, and that he would give her the proper civil amount of commiseration for her ailments, which every guest ought to bestow upon a hostess who complains of her delicacy of health
point: lunch を補語と見たり、後半の thought that ~ や which every guest ought to bestow（SVO）を判定したりしやすい。主節は There was lunch の存在文。第1文型。
explanation: There is 構文で There は M、主語は lunch。SV。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: When the grass required his close attention, or when he had to stoop to cut about a head-stone, he paused in his lively air,—the “Jewel” song,—taking it up where he had left it when his scythe swung free again.
translation: 草を念入りに刈らねばならないときや、墓石のまわりを刈るためにかがまねばならないとき、彼は陽気な歌――「宝石の歌」――を中断し、また鎌が自由に振れるようになると、やめたところから歌い直した。
parts: When the grass required his close attention, or when he had to stoop to cut about a head-stone
taking it up where he had left it when his scythe swung free again
point: when 節の required his close attention、stoop to cut や、taking it up（SVO）に目的語があるので、第3文型を選びやすい。主節は he paused（立ち止まった）で、pause は自動詞。第1文型。
explanation: pause「途中で止める」は自動詞で、in his lively air は M。SV。
author: Willa Cather
authorJa: ウィラ・キャザー

text: She looked fixedly up the bleak street as if she were gathering her strength to face something, as if she were trying with all her might to grasp a situation which, no matter how painful, must be met and dealt with somehow.
translation: 彼女は寒々とした通りの先をじっと見つめた。何かに立ち向かうために力を集めているかのように、どれほどつらくても何とかして向き合い、片をつけねばならない事態を、全力でつかもうとしているかのように。
parts: as if she were gathering her strength to face something, as if she were trying with all her might to grasp a situation which, no matter how painful, must be met and dealt with somehow
point: look は「〜に見える」の第2文型にもなるので、as if 節を補語と見て第2文型を選びやすい。ここは「〜のような様子で見た」で、as if 節は様態の修飾語。gathering ... to face ~ なども修飾語。She looked で第1文型。
explanation: look は自動詞、up the bleak street の up は前置詞。SV。
author: Willa Cather
authorJa: ウィラ・キャザー

text: Hetty answered with a dimpled smile, as if she did not quite know what had been said; and it made a strange contrast to see that sparkling self-engrossed loveliness looked at by Dinah’s calm pitying face, with its open glance which told that her heart lived in no cherished secrets of its own, but in feelings which it longed to share with all the world.
target: Hetty answered with a dimpled smile, as if she did not quite know what had been said
translation: ヘティは何を言われたのかよくわからないかのように、えくぼを浮かべてほほえんで答えた。きらきらした、自分のことしか頭にないその愛らしさが、ダイナの穏やかな憐れみの顔に見つめられているのは奇妙な対照だった。ダイナの開いたまなざしは、彼女の心が自分だけの大事な秘密に生きているのではなく、世のすべての人と分かちあいたいと願う感情に生きていることを物語っていた。
parts: as if she did not quite know what had been said
point: answer は「〜に答える」の他動詞にもなるので、後ろに目的語を探しやすい。また後半の it made a strange contrast to see ~ や which told that ~ にもつられる。Hetty answered with a smile で第1文型。
explanation: answer は目的語なしの自動詞として使われ、with 句と as if 節は M。判定部分は SV。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: He was frequently met in the lanes by pedestrians and others without his seeing them, and by degrees the people of the neighbourhood began to talk about his method of combining work and play (such they considered his reading to be), which, though probably convenient enough to himself, was not altogether a safe proceeding for other travellers along the same roads.
target: He was frequently met in the lanes by pedestrians and others without his seeing them
translation: 彼は小道で歩行者などに出会われることがしばしばあったが、本人は相手に気づかなかった。やがて近所の人々は、仕事と遊び（彼らは彼の読書をそう考えていた）を一緒にする彼のやり方を噂しはじめた。それは本人にはさぞ便利だったのだろうが、同じ道を行くほかの者にとってはあまり安全なやり方ではなかった。
parts: by pedestrians and others without his seeing them
point: meet は「〜に会う」の他動詞なので第3文型を選びやすい。しかしこの文は受動態（be met by 〜）で、目的語は残らない。without his seeing them や began to talk も修飾語の中。第1文型。
explanation: meet の受動態で、後ろは by 句などの修飾語だけ。判定部分は SV（後半は別の文）。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: Here was a corps of teachers and masters, more stringently tasked, as all the real head-labour was to be done by them, in order to save the pupils, yet having their duties so arranged that they relieved each other in quick succession whenever the work was severe: here, in short, was a foreign school; of which the life, movement, and variety made it a complete and most charming contrast to many English institutions of the same kind.
translation: ここには男女の教師陣がいて、本当の頭の仕事はすべて彼らが担い、生徒の負担を軽くするようになっているので、より厳しく働かされていた。それでも仕事がきついときにはすぐに交代できるよう、務めが割り振られていた。要するに、ここは外国の学校だった。その活気と動きと多彩さによって、同じ種類の多くのイギリスの学校とはまったく対照的な、実に魅力ある場所になっていた。
parts: a corps of teachers and masters

more stringently tasked, as all the real head-labour was to be done by them, in order to save the pupils, yet having their duties so arranged that they relieved each other in quick succession whenever the work was severe
of which the life, movement, and variety made it a complete and most charming contrast to many English institutions of the same kind
point: a corps of teachers を補語と見たり、having their duties so arranged that ~ や made it a contrast（SVOC）を判定したりしやすい。主節は There was＋主語の存在文が2つ。第1文型。
explanation: Here was 〜「ここに〜がいた」は倒置で、Here は M、主語は corps と school。SV が2つ。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: Mrs. Hamley came a little forwards to meet her, and introduced her in so fondly intimate a way to her son, that Molly, innocent and simple, knowing nothing but Hollingford manners, which were anything but formal, half put out her hand to shake hands with one of whom she had heard so much--the son of such kind friends.
target: Mrs. Hamley came a little forwards to meet her
translation: ハムリー夫人は少し前へ出て彼女を迎え、ひどく親しげに息子に引き合わせた。それでモリーは、うぶで素直で、少しも堅苦しくないホリングフォードの作法しか知らなかったので、あれほど話に聞いていた人――あれほど親切な友人たちの息子――と握手しようと、思わず手を半分差し出した。
point: to meet her を come の目的語と見て、第3文型を選びやすい。これは目的の不定詞で修飾語。後半の so 〜 that 構文や関係詞節も長い。Mrs. Hamley came で第1文型。
explanation: come は自動詞、a little forwards と to meet her は M。判定部分は SV（and introduced her ... は SVO）。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: And then the day came back to him when he was a little fellow and used to run by his father’s side, proud to be taken out to work, and prouder still to hear his father boasting to his fellow-workmen how “the little chap had an uncommon notion o’ carpentering.”
translation: そして彼の心に、幼い日のことがよみがえった。父のそばを走って、仕事に連れて行ってもらうのが誇らしく、父が仕事仲間に「このちびは大工仕事のこつがめっぽうわかってる」と自慢するのを聞くのがさらに誇らしかった日々のことが。
parts: when he was a little fellow and used to run by his father’s side, proud to be taken out to work, and prouder still to hear his father boasting to his fellow-workmen how “the little chap had an uncommon notion o’ carpentering.”
point: when 節が先行詞 the day から離れていて、その中の used to run、hear his father boasting（SVOC）を判定しやすい。主節は the day came back to him で、come back は自動詞。第1文型。
explanation: come back「戻ってくる・思い出される」は自動詞。SV。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: Meanwhile Henchard was sitting up, thinking over his jealous folly in forbidding Farfrae to pay his addresses to this girl who did not belong to him, when if he had allowed them to go on he might not have been encumbered with her.
translation: 一方ヘンチャードは寝ずに起きていて、自分のものでもないこの娘にファーフレイが言い寄るのを禁じた嫉妬深い愚かさを思い返していた。二人をそのままにしておけば、彼女を抱えこまずにすんだかもしれないのに。
parts: thinking over his jealous folly in forbidding Farfrae to pay his addresses to this girl who did not belong to him, when if he had allowed them to go on he might not have been encumbered with her
point: sit up は自動詞なので目的語がないが、forbidding Farfrae to pay（forbid O to do）や allowed them to go on（SVOC）に引っぱられて第5文型を選びやすい。主節は Henchard was sitting up で第1文型。
explanation: sit up「寝ずに起きている」は自動詞。SV。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: カスターブリッジの市長

text: Just as I was beginning to hope that the mate would come out calmer--for I heard him knocking away at something in the hold, and work is good for him--there came up the hatchway a sudden, startled scream, which made my blood run cold, and up on the deck he came as if shot from a gun--a raging madman, with his eyes rolling and his face convulsed with fear.
translation: 航海士が少し落ち着いて出てくるのではないかと期待しはじめたちょうどそのとき――船倉で何かをたたいている音が聞こえていたし、働くのは彼のためになるのだ――昇降口から、突然ぎょっとしたような悲鳴が上がり、私の血は凍りついた。そして彼は鉄砲で撃ち出されたかのように甲板に飛び出してきた――目をぎょろつかせ、恐怖で顔をひきつらせた、荒れ狂う狂人となって。
parts: Just as I was beginning to hope that the mate would come out calmer
for I heard him knocking away at something in the hold, and work is good for him
which made my blood run cold
as if shot from a gun--a raging madman, with his eyes rolling and his face convulsed with fear
point: heard him knocking（知覚動詞）や which made my blood run cold（SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。また倒置の came a sudden scream、up on the deck he came で主語を見失う。どちらも came の第1文型。
explanation: there came 〜「〜が来た」は There 構文の一種で、主語は scream。後半も come の自動詞。SV が2つ。
author: Bram Stoker
authorJa: ブラム・ストーカー

text: If you were to meet all day with people who care absolutely nothing about you, if you went day after day to a place where there was nothing but show and indifference, if there was not one person in all those you knew to whom you could appeal for sympathy or talk to with pleasure, perhaps you would be unhappy too.”
translation: もしあなたが一日じゅう自分のことなど少しも気にかけない人たちと会っていたら、見せびらかしと無関心しかない場所へ毎日毎日通っていたら、知り合いのだれ一人として同情を求めたり楽しく話したりできる相手がいなかったら、たぶんあなたも不幸になるでしょう。
parts: If you were to meet all day with people who care absolutely nothing about you, if you went day after day to a place where there was nothing but show and indifference, if there was not one person in all those you knew to whom you could appeal for sympathy or talk to with pleasure
point: if 節が3つ並び、care nothing about you、to whom you could appeal ~ などに気を取られて主節を見失いやすい。主節は you would be unhappy で、you＝unhappy の第2文型。
explanation: 主節は you would be unhappy。unhappy が主語の状態を表す補語。SVC。
author: Theodore Dreiser
authorJa: セオドア・ドライサー

text: It amounted to nearly a thousand a year; when she reflected on its extent, her dearest hope was to hand it over, not only unimpaired but increased, to her husband's son, to her own darling, to the little man who now lay sleeping on her knee, happily ignorant of the cares which were to be accumulated in his behalf.
target: her dearest hope was to hand it over, not only unimpaired but increased, to her husband's son, to her own darling, to the little man who now lay sleeping on her knee, happily ignorant of the cares which were to be accumulated in his behalf
translation: それは年に千ポンド近くになった。その額を思うと、彼女のいちばんの願いは、それを損なわないばかりか増やしたうえで、夫の息子に、自分の大切な子に、いま膝の上で眠っている小さな男の子に引き渡すことだった。この子は自分のために積み重ねられることになる気苦労など、幸いにも何も知らなかった。
parts: to hand it over, not only unimpaired but increased, to her husband's son, to her own darling, to the little man who now lay sleeping on her knee, happily ignorant of the cares which were to be accumulated in his behalf
point: 補語の to hand it over を見て、hand it（SVO）から第3文型を選びやすい。また not only unimpaired but increased を補語と見る誤りもある。不定詞全体が補語。hope was to hand ~ の第2文型。
explanation: 主語 hope の中身を to hand it over が説明する。名詞用法の不定詞が補語の SVC。
author: Anthony Trollope
authorJa: アントニー・トロロープ

text: It was not the convention of the meeting to say good-bye, or necessarily even to nod to the person with whom one was talking; but, nevertheless, Denham was disappointed by the completeness with which Katharine parted from him, without any attempt to finish her sentence.
target: It was not the convention of the meeting to say good-bye, or necessarily even to nod to the person with whom one was talking
translation: その集まりでは、さよならを言うことも、話していた相手にうなずくことさえも、必ずしも決まりではなかった。それでもデナムは、キャサリンが言いかけた言葉を終えようともせず、あまりにもきっぱりと彼のもとを離れたことにがっかりした。
parts: to say good-bye, or necessarily even to nod to the person with whom one was talking
point: It を本当の主語と思うと、to say good-bye の扱いに困って構造を見失いやすい。また the person with whom ~ にもつられる。It は仮主語で、真主語は to say ~ / to nod。It＝the convention の第2文型。
explanation: It（=to say ...）was the convention。名詞の補語をとる SVC。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: It’s very blessed on a bleak cold day, when the sky is hanging dark over the hill, to feel the love of God in one’s soul, and carry it to the lonely, bare, stone houses, where there’s nothing else to give comfort.”
translation: 空が丘の上に暗く垂れこめている寒々しい冷たい日に、魂の中に神の愛を感じ、それをほかに慰めになるものが何もない、ぽつんと建つ寒々とした石の家々へ運んでいくのは、とても恵まれたことなのです。
parts: when the sky is hanging dark over the hill
to feel the love of God in one’s soul, and carry it to the lonely, bare, stone houses, where there’s nothing else to give comfort
point: It を本当の主語と思うと、to feel the love of God（SVO）を判定しやすい。また where there's nothing else to give comfort にもつられる。It は仮主語で、真主語は不定詞。It＝blessed の第2文型。
explanation: It is blessed to do「〜するのは恵まれたことだ」。形容詞が補語の SVC。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: Being proposed to is all very nice and all that sort of thing, but it isn’t at all a happy thing when you have to see a poor fellow, whom you know loves you honestly, going away and looking all broken-hearted, and to know that, no matter what he may say at the moment, you are passing quite out of his life.
target: Being proposed to is all very nice and all that sort of thing
translation: 結婚を申し込まれるのは、まあとてもすてきなことではあるけれど、自分を真剣に愛してくれているとわかっている気の毒な人が、すっかり打ちひしがれた様子で去っていくのを見なければならず、しかも相手がそのとき何を言おうと、自分はもうその人の人生から完全に出ていこうとしているのだとわかっているのは、ちっとも幸せなことではない。
parts: and all that sort of thing
point: Being proposed to（受動態の動名詞）を動詞と見て、主語を見失いやすい。また see a poor fellow going away（SVOC）にもつられる。動名詞の句が主語で、is all very nice の第2文型。
explanation: 動名詞句が主語、nice が補語。and all that sort of thing「その他もろもろ」は添え物。判定部分は SVC。
author: Bram Stoker
authorJa: ブラム・ストーカー

text: The very merchants whose droning she found the dullest at the two or three parties which were given to welcome her were the pleasantest confidants of all when they had something to talk about--lemons or cotton voile or floor-oil.
translation: 彼女を歓迎するために開かれた二、三のパーティーで、その単調なおしゃべりがいちばん退屈だと思ったまさにその商人たちが、話すこと――レモンや木綿のボイルや床用の油――があるときには、だれよりも気持ちのいい打ち明け相手だった。
parts: whose droning she found the dullest at the two or three parties which were given to welcome her
when they had something to talk about--lemons or cotton voile or floor-oil
point: 関係詞節の whose droning she found the dullest（find O C）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これは merchants を修飾する部分。The merchants were the pleasantest confidants で第2文型。
explanation: 主語 merchants と補語 confidants がイコール関係。SVC。
author: Sinclair Lewis
authorJa: シンクレア・ルイス

text: It seems plain that schemers would choose more sequestered quarters to arrange their plans, that politicians would not gather here in company to discuss anything save formalities, where the sharp-eared may hear, and it would scarcely be justified on the score of thirst, for the majority of those who frequent these more gorgeous places have no craving for liquor.
target: It seems plain that schemers would choose more sequestered quarters to arrange their plans, that politicians would not gather here in company to discuss anything save formalities, where the sharp-eared may hear
translation: 陰謀をめぐらす者なら計画を練るのにもっと人目につかない場所を選ぶだろうし、政治家なら耳ざとい者に聞かれかねないこんな所に連れ立って集まって、形式的なこと以外を話しあったりはしないだろう。それは明らかに思われる。また喉の渇きを理由にするのもとうてい無理だ。こうした豪華な場所に通う者の大半は、酒を欲しがってなどいないのだから。
parts: that schemers would choose more sequestered quarters to arrange their plans, that politicians would not gather here in company to discuss anything save formalities, where the sharp-eared may hear
point: It を本当の主語と思うと、that 節の中の would choose ~（SVO）を判定しやすい。It は仮主語で、真主語は2つの that 節。seem は「〜に見える」で、It＝plain の第2文型。
explanation: seem「〜に思われる」は第2文型の動詞で、plain が補語。SVC。
author: Theodore Dreiser
authorJa: セオドア・ドライサー

text: In short, they were the kind of letters a young man writes to a woman when he wishes himself and his life to seem interesting to her, when he wishes to enlist her imagination in his behalf.
translation: 要するにそれは、若い男が女に自分と自分の人生を面白いものに見せたいとき、自分のために女の想像力を引き寄せたいときに書くたぐいの手紙だった。
parts: a young man writes to a woman when he wishes himself and his life to seem interesting to her, when he wishes to enlist her imagination in his behalf
point: 関係詞節の中の wishes himself and his life to seem interesting（wish O to do）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これは letters を修飾する部分。they were the kind of letters で第2文型。
explanation: 主語 they（=letters）と the kind of letters がイコール。SVC。
author: Willa Cather
authorJa: ウィラ・キャザー

text: The stair had been carried no higher; to set a stranger mounting it in the darkness was to send him straight to his death; and (although, thanks to the lightning and my own precautions, I was safe enough) the mere thought of the peril in which I might have stood, and the dreadful height I might have fallen from, brought out the sweat upon my body and relaxed my joints.
target: to set a stranger mounting it in the darkness was to send him straight to his death
translation: 階段はそれより上には作られていなかった。見知らぬ者を暗がりの中でこれを上らせるのは、まっすぐ死へ送りこむことだった。そして（稲妻と自分の用心のおかげで十分安全だったとはいえ）自分が置かれていたかもしれない危険と、落ちていたかもしれない恐ろしい高さを思っただけで、体に汗が噴き出し、関節の力が抜けた。
parts: to set a stranger mounting it in the darkness
to send him straight to his death
point: 主語の to set a stranger mounting it（set O -ing）や補語の to send him straight to his death（SVO）が目立つので、第5文型や第3文型を選びやすい。主語も補語も不定詞。to set ~ was to send ~ の第2文型。
explanation: 「〜することは…することだった」。不定詞が主語と補語になる SVC。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン
workJa: さらわれたデービッド

text: I tried to get this out of my head; but though I took down many interesting authors, old and new, history, poetry, and story-book, this notion of my father’s hand of writing stuck to me; and when at length I went back into the kitchen, and sat down once more to porridge and small beer, the first thing I said to Uncle Ebenezer was to ask him if my father had not been very quick at his book.
target: the first thing I said to Uncle Ebenezer was to ask him if my father had not been very quick at his book
translation: 私はこのことを頭から追い払おうとした。だが新旧の面白い著者の本――歴史、詩、物語の本――をたくさん手に取ったのに、父の筆跡のことが頭から離れなかった。そしてようやく台所に戻り、ふたたびオートミールのかゆと弱いビールの前に腰を下ろすと、エベニーザー叔父に最初に口にしたのは、父はとても勉強がよくできたのではないかと尋ねることだった。
parts: to ask him if my father had not been very quick at his book
point: 補語の to ask him if ~ が ask O1 O2（第4文型）の形なので、第4文型を選びやすい。また主語の the first thing I said も紛らわしい。不定詞全体が補語。thing was to ask ~ の第2文型。
explanation: 主語 thing の中身を to ask ... が説明する SVC。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン
workJa: さらわれたデービッド

text: For a novel addressed by a man to men and women of full age, which attempts to deal unaffectedly with the fret and fever, derision and disaster, that may press in the wake of the strongest passion known to humanity, and to point, without a mincing of words, the tragedy of unfulfilled aims, I am not aware that there is anything in the handling to which exception can be taken.
translation: 人間に知られている最も強い情熱のあとに押し寄せかねない苛立ちと熱狂、嘲りと災いを気取らずに扱い、言葉を飾らずに、果たされなかった望みの悲劇を指し示そうとする、男が成熟した男女に向けて書いた小説として、その扱いに異議を唱えられるような点があるとは私は思わない。
parts: For a novel addressed by a man to men and women of full age, which attempts to deal unaffectedly with the fret and fever, derision and disaster, that may press in the wake of the strongest passion known to humanity, and to point, without a mincing of words, the tragedy of unfulfilled aims
that there is anything in the handling to which exception can be taken
point: aware の後ろの of anything ... to which exception can be taken や、a novel which attempts to deal ~ に気を取られやすい。be aware of 〜 の aware は形容詞で補語。I am not aware の第2文型。
explanation: be aware「気づいている」で aware が補語。that 節は aware の内容を示す修飾語。SVC。
note: be aware that 〜 をひとまとまりの他動詞のように見て that 節を目的語とする説明もあるが、学校文法では形容詞＋that 節で SVC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: It was enough to put a man a little out, let him have been ever so used to pulpit reading, to see the knowing way in which the farmers cocked their ears and set about a mental criticism as to whether their new minister did or did not fall short of the excellence of him who had lately departed from them.
translation: たとえどれほど説教壇での朗読に慣れていたとしても、農夫たちが心得顔で耳をそばだて、新しい牧師が最近去った前任者の見事さに及ぶか及ばないかを頭の中で品定めしはじめる様子を見るのは、人を少々まごつかせるに十分だった。
parts: enough to put a man a little out
let him have been ever so used to pulpit reading

to see the knowing way in which the farmers cocked their ears and set about a mental criticism as to whether their new minister did or did not fall short of the excellence of him who had lately departed from them
point: It を本当の主語と思うと、enough to put a man a little out や to see the knowing way ~ の扱いに困って構造を見失いやすい。It は仮主語で、真主語は to see ~。It＝enough to put ~ の第2文型。
explanation: It（=to see ...）was enough。形容詞 enough が補語の SVC。
author: Anthony Trollope
authorJa: アントニー・トロロープ

text: When his reverses first began it had seemed easy for him to give up everything, to let the people he owed take all, so only they would let him go out with clean hands; and he had dramatised this feeling in his talk with his wife, when they spoke together of the mills on the G.
target: When his reverses first began it had seemed easy for him to give up everything, to let the people he owed take all, so only they would let him go out with clean hands
translation: 逆境が始まったばかりのころは、すべてを手放し、借りのある人々に何もかも取らせて、そのかわり潔白な手で出ていかせてもらえさえすればよい、と思うのはたやすいことに思えた。そして彼はこの気持ちを、G 社の工場のことを話しあったとき、妻との会話の中で芝居がかって語っていた。
parts: to give up everything, to let the people he owed take all, so only they would let him go out with clean hands
point: it を本当の主語と思うと、真主語の to give up everything や let the people take all（SVOC）を判定しやすい。it は仮主語で、真主語は不定詞の2つ。seem は「〜に見える」で、it＝easy の第2文型。
explanation: seem の後ろの easy が補語。SVC。
author: William Dean Howells
authorJa: W・D・ハウエルズ
workJa: サイラス・ラパムの出世

text: Mrs. Costello was a widow with a fortune; a person of much distinction, who frequently intimated that, if she were not so dreadfully liable to sick headaches, she would probably have left a deeper impress upon her time.
translation: コステロ夫人は財産のある未亡人で、ひどく名の通った人だった。もしあれほど頭痛を起こしやすい体質でなかったら、自分の時代にもっと深い足跡を残していただろう、としばしばほのめかしていた。
parts: a person of much distinction, who frequently intimated that, if she were not so dreadfully liable to sick headaches, she would probably have left a deeper impress upon her time
point: a person of much distinction を2つ目の要素と見て第5文型を選んだり、who 節の中の仮定法を判定したりしやすい。これは a widow の言い換え（同格）。Mrs. Costello was a widow の第2文型。
explanation: 主語と a widow がイコール。セミコロン以下も同じ補語の言い換え。SVC。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: When he had gone on to give details which a whole series of slight and unregarded incidents in her past life strangely corroborated; when, in short, she believed his story to be true, she became greatly agitated, and turning round to the table flung her face upon it weeping.
translation: 彼が話を続けて、彼女の過去の、取るに足らない、気にも留めなかった数々の出来事が不思議にも裏づける詳しいことを語り、要するに彼女がその話を本当だと信じたとき、彼女はひどく取り乱し、テーブルの方へ向き直ると、そこに顔を伏せて泣いた。
parts: When he had gone on to give details which a whole series of slight and unregarded incidents in her past life strangely corroborated; when, in short, she believed his story to be true
and turning round to the table flung her face upon it weeping
point: agitated を受動態の過去分詞と見て、第1文型を選びやすい。また believed his story to be true（SVOC）にもつられる。become＋形容詞化した過去分詞で、she＝agitated。第2文型。
explanation: become は第2文型の動詞で、agitated（過去分詞の形容詞）が補語。SVC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: カスターブリッジの市長

text: I am sure if they ask me--which certainly they ought to do--I won't say before they asked Cynthia, because I never think of myself, and am really the most forgiving person in the world, in forgiving slights;--but when they do ask me, which they are sure to do, I shall never be content till, by putting in a little hint here and a little hint there, I've induced them to send you an invitation.
target: I shall never be content till, by putting in a little hint here and a little hint there, I've induced them to send you an invitation
translation: きっとあちらが私を招いてくれたら――当然そうすべきだけれど――シンシアより先にとは言わないわ、私は自分のことなど考えないし、軽んじられても許してあげる、ほんとうに世界一寛大な人間なんですもの――でもあちらが私を招いたら、きっとそうするに決まっているけど、あちこちで少しずつほのめかして、あなたにも招待状を出させるまでは、私、決して満足しないわ。
parts: till, by putting in a little hint here and a little hint there, I've induced them to send you an invitation
point: by putting in a little hint や induced them to send you an invitation（SVOC の中に SVOO）が目立つので、第5文型や第4文型を選びやすい。主節は I shall never be content で、I＝content の第2文型。
explanation: be content「満足している」。till 以下は時の副詞節。SVC。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: Mrs. Walker was one of those American ladies who, while residing abroad, make a point, in their own phrase, of studying European society, and she had on this occasion collected several specimens of her diversely born fellow mortals to serve, as it were, as textbooks.
target: Mrs. Walker was one of those American ladies who, while residing abroad, make a point, in their own phrase, of studying European society
translation: ウォーカー夫人は、外国に住むあいだ、彼女たち自身の言い方を借りれば「ヨーロッパの社交界を研究すること」を心がけている、あのアメリカ婦人たちの一人で、このときも、いわば教科書として役立てるために、生まれもさまざまな人間の見本を何人か集めていた。
parts: who, while residing abroad, make a point, in their own phrase, of studying European society
point: 関係詞節の make a point of studying（make a point of -ing）や while residing abroad に気を取られやすい。それは ladies を修飾する部分。Mrs. Walker was one of those ladies で第2文型。
explanation: 主語 Mrs. Walker と one（=a lady）がイコール。判定部分は SVC（後半は別の SVO）。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: He was a stout florid man about forty years of age, who surveyed people up and down when first making their acquaintance, and generally smiled at the horizon or other distant object during conversations with friends, walking about with a steady sway, and turning out his toes very considerably.
translation: 彼は四十歳ほどの太った赤ら顔の男で、初めて知り合うときには相手を上から下までじろじろ眺め、友人と話しているときはたいてい地平線か何か遠くのものに向かってほほえみ、しっかりと体を揺らして、ひどくつま先を外に向けて歩いた。
parts: about forty years of age, who surveyed people up and down when first making their acquaintance, and generally smiled at the horizon or other distant object during conversations with friends, walking about with a steady sway, and turning out his toes very considerably
point: 関係詞節の surveyed ~（SVO）や walking about ... and turning out his toes に目的語があるので、第3文型を選びやすい。それは man を修飾する部分。He was a stout florid man で第2文型。
explanation: 主語 He と a ... man がイコール。SVC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: But although she was silent, she was evidently mistress of a situation which was familiar enough to her, and inclined to let it take its way for the six hundredth time, perhaps, without bringing into play any of her unoccupied faculties.
translation: しかし彼女は黙っていたけれど、明らかに、自分にはすっかりなじみの状況を取りしきっていて、使われていない能力をどれひとつ持ち出すこともなく、おそらく六百回目になるだろうが、成り行きにまかせるつもりでいた。
parts: which was familiar enough to her
and inclined to let it take its way for the six hundredth time, perhaps, without bringing into play any of her unoccupied faculties
point: inclined を過去分詞の動詞と見たり、let it take its way（SVOC）を判定したりしやすい。また bringing into play unoccupied faculties も紛らわしい。mistress と inclined がともに補語。she was ~ の第2文型。
explanation: was の補語が mistress of ... と inclined to ... の2つ。SVC。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: She was fond of the little girls, especially of Milly, who came to spend a week with her aunt now and then, and read aloud to her from the old books about the house, or listened to stories about the early days on the Divide.
translation: 彼女は小さな女の子たち、とくにミリーをかわいがっていた。ミリーはときどき一週間ほど伯母のところに泊まりに来て、家にある古い本を読んで聞かせたり、ディヴァイドの開拓初期の話に耳を傾けたりした。
parts: of the little girls, especially of Milly, who came to spend a week with her aunt now and then, and read aloud to her from the old books about the house, or listened to stories about the early days on the Divide
point: 挿入の who came to spend a week ... and read aloud（目的語あり）を判定して、第3文型を選びやすい。それは Milly を説明する部分。be fond of 〜 の fond は形容詞で補語。She was fond の第2文型。
explanation: be fond of 〜「〜を好む」で fond が補語、of 以下は M。SVC。
author: Willa Cather
authorJa: ウィラ・キャザー

text: Finally, however, they had found courage to enter, and duly met Stannidge the landlord, a silent man, who drew and carried frothing measures to this room and to that, shoulder to shoulder with his waiting-maids—a stately slowness, however, entering into his ministrations by contrast with theirs, as became one whose service was somewhat optional.
translation: しかし結局、彼らは思い切って中に入り、きちんと主人のスタニッジに会った。無口な男で、泡立つ酒を注いでは、女給たちと肩を並べてこちらの部屋あちらの部屋へと運んでいた。もっとも、彼の給仕には、女給たちと比べて堂々としたゆっくりさがあった。務めがいくぶん気まぐれでよい者にふさわしいことだった。
parts: Stannidge the landlord, a silent man, who drew and carried frothing measures to this room and to that, shoulder to shoulder with his waiting-maids—a stately slowness, however, entering into his ministrations by contrast with theirs, as became one whose service was somewhat optional
point: courage to enter の不定詞や、a stately slowness ... entering into ~（独立分詞構文）、as became one ~ に気を取られやすい。また同格の言い換えで目的語が2つに見える。found courage / met Stannidge で第3文型。
explanation: find courage「勇気を出す」、meet Stannidge と、目的語をとる動詞が2つ。SVO。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: カスターブリッジの市長

text: And he desired more and more to make it a certainty that he was to have the privilege of a tete-a-tete with the young lady, who was still strolling along in front of them, softly vocalizing.
translation: そして彼は、まだ前をぶらぶら歩きながら小声で歌っているその若い娘と二人きりで話す特権に自分があずかれることを、ますます確かなものにしたいと思った。
parts: to make it a certainty that he was to have the privilege of a tete-a-tete with the young lady, who was still strolling along in front of them, softly vocalizing
point: 不定詞の中の make it a certainty that ~（形式目的語の SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これは目的語の中身。desire の目的語は to make ~ の不定詞全体。第3文型。
explanation: desire to do「〜したいと強く思う」。不定詞が目的語の SVO。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: She recalled a hundred grotesqueries: her comic dismay at his having chewed tobacco, the evening when she had tried to read poetry to him; matters which had seemed to vanish with no trace or sequence.
translation: 彼女はおかしなことを数かぎりなく思い出した。彼が噛みたばこを噛んでいたのを知ったときの自分のおどけた狼狽、彼に詩を読んで聞かせようとした晩――跡形も脈絡もなく消えてしまったように思えていた出来事を。
parts: her comic dismay at his having chewed tobacco, the evening when she had tried to read poetry to him; matters which had seemed to vanish with no trace or sequence
point: コロンのあとの her comic dismay を2つ目の目的語と見て、第4文型を選びやすい。これは grotesqueries の具体例（同格）。また tried to read poetry to him にもつられる。recalled grotesqueries で第3文型。
explanation: recall「思い出す」の目的語が grotesqueries（とその言い換え）。SVO。
author: Sinclair Lewis
authorJa: シンクレア・ルイス

text: Hurstwood was a man of authority and some fine feeling, and it irritated him excessively to find himself surrounded more and more by a world upon which he had no hold, and of which he had a lessening understanding.
target: it irritated him excessively to find himself surrounded more and more by a world upon which he had no hold, and of which he had a lessening understanding
translation: ハーストウッドは権威があり、それなりに繊細な感情も持った男だったので、自分の力の及ばない世界、しかもだんだん理解できなくなっていく世界にますます取り囲まれていると気づくのは、ひどく腹立たしいことだった。
parts: to find himself surrounded more and more by a world upon which he had no hold, and of which he had a lessening understanding
point: it を本当の主語と思うと、真主語の to find himself surrounded（find O 過去分詞の SVOC）が目立って第5文型を選びやすい。it は仮主語で、真主語は不定詞。irritated him で第3文型。
explanation: irritate「いらだたせる」の目的語が him。仮主語構文の SVO。
author: Theodore Dreiser
authorJa: セオドア・ドライサー

text: It was only when I told him that we should want him to help us during the day, and that we must not all break down for want of rest, lest Lucy should suffer, that he agreed to go.
translation: 昼間に私たちを手伝ってもらいたいし、ルーシーのためにも、休息が足りなくて皆が倒れるわけにはいかない、と私が言ってやってはじめて、彼は行くことを承知した。
parts: I told him that we should want him to help us during the day, and that we must not all break down for want of rest, lest Lucy should suffer
point: It was only when ... that 〜 の強調構文で、It was を第2文型と見たり、told him that ... and that ~（SVOO）を判定したりしやすい。強調を外すと He agreed to go only when ~。agree の目的語が不定詞の第3文型。
explanation: 強調構文は元の文で判定する。agree to do「〜することに同意する」で不定詞が目的語。SVO。
note: agree は自動詞で to go を副詞的に見る立場もあるが、学校文法では to 不定詞を目的語とする SVO。
author: Bram Stoker
authorJa: ブラム・ストーカー

text: She did not like the morning cup of coffee; its school brewage not being strong or sweet enough to suit her palate; and she had an excellent appetite, like any other healthy school-girl, for the morning pistolets or rolls, which were new-baked and very good, and of which a certain allowance was served to each.
translation: 彼女は朝のコーヒーが好きではなかった。学校でいれるものは、口に合うほど濃くも甘くもなかったからだ。そして、ほかの元気な女生徒と同じく、朝のピストレつまりロールパンには旺盛な食欲を見せた。ロールパンは焼きたてでとてもおいしく、一人ひとりに決まった数が出された。
parts: its school brewage not being strong or sweet enough to suit her palate
an excellent appetite, like any other healthy school-girl, for the morning pistolets or rolls, which were new-baked and very good, and of which a certain allowance was served to each
point: 独立分詞構文 its school brewage not being strong enough to suit ~ や関係詞節が長く、動詞を見失いやすい。また like any other ~ を補語と見る誤りもある。did not like the coffee / had an appetite で第3文型。
explanation: like coffee と had an excellent appetite。目的語をとる SVO が2つ。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: Not being quite tall enough to lift my head over his desk, elevated upon the estrade, and thus suffering eclipse in my present position, I ventured to peep round, with the design, at first, of merely getting a better view of his face, which had struck me when I entered as bearing a close and picturesque resemblance to that of a black and sallow tiger.
translation: 高い壇の上の彼の机越しに頭を出すほど背が高くなく、そのため今の場所では陰に隠れてしまうので、私は思い切ってのぞいてみた。最初はただ、彼の顔をもっとよく見たいだけのつもりだった。その顔は、入ってきたとき、黒く黄ばんだ虎の顔にそっくりで絵のようだと思ったのだ。
parts: Not being quite tall enough to lift my head over his desk, elevated upon the estrade, and thus suffering eclipse in my present position
with the design, at first, of merely getting a better view of his face, which had struck me when I entered as bearing a close and picturesque resemblance to that of a black and sallow tiger
point: venture は「危険を冒して行く」の自動詞の印象もあり、また Not being quite tall enough to lift ~ や strike O as 〜 に気を取られやすい。venture to do（思いきって〜する）の不定詞が目的語。第3文型。
explanation: venture to do「思い切って〜する」で不定詞が目的語。SVO。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: Being, as they were, rather large and conveniently situated in a street mostly dedicated to offices off the Strand, people who wished to meet, either for purposes of enjoyment, or to discuss art, or to reform the State, had a way of suggesting that Mary had better be asked to lend them her rooms.
translation: メアリーの部屋はかなり広く、ストランド街から少し入った、ほとんど事務所ばかりの通りという便利な所にあったので、楽しみのためであれ、芸術を論じるためであれ、国家を改革するためであれ、集まりたい人々は、メアリーに部屋を貸してくれと頼んだらいい、と言い出すのが常だった。
parts: Being, as they were, rather large and conveniently situated in a street mostly dedicated to offices off the Strand
who wished to meet, either for purposes of enjoyment, or to discuss art, or to reform the State
a way of suggesting that Mary had better be asked to lend them her rooms
point: Being, as they were, rather large ~ の分詞構文や、that 節の中の be asked to lend（ask O to do の受動）に気を取られやすい。have a way of -ing（〜する癖がある）。目的語 a way の第3文型。
explanation: have a way of -ing「〜するのが常だ」。have の目的語が a way。SVO。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: Lapham took refuge in trying to think who the party could be; he concluded that it must have been somebody who had gone over it with the architect, and he did not like that; but he was aware that this was not an answer to the broker, and he wrote that he would give him an answer in the morning.
target: Lapham took refuge in trying to think who the party could be
translation: ラパムは、その相手がだれなのかを考えようとすることに逃げこんだ。建築家と一緒に家を見て回った人に違いないと結論を下したが、それは気に入らなかった。けれどもそれでは仲買人への返事にならないとわかっていたので、明朝返事をすると書いた。
parts: in trying to think who the party could be
point: take refuge in 〜 の in trying to think を2つ目の要素と見て、第5文型を選びやすい。また後半の give him an answer（SVOO）にもつられる。in 以下は前置詞句。took refuge の第3文型。
explanation: take refuge in 〜「〜に逃げこむ」。take の目的語が refuge。判定部分は SVO。
author: William Dean Howells
authorJa: W・D・ハウエルズ
workJa: サイラス・ラパムの出世

text: She tried to make herself something to do, but that beauty, which she had not liked, followed her amid the work of overhauling the summer clothing, which Irene had seen to putting away in the fall.
translation: 彼女は何かすることを自分でこしらえようとしたが、好きになれなかったあの美しさが、夏服の手入れをするあいだもつきまとってきた。夏服は、秋にアイリーンがしまうのを見届けておいたものだった。
parts: to make herself something to do
but that beauty, which she had not liked, followed her amid the work of overhauling the summer clothing, which Irene had seen to putting away in the fall
point: 不定詞の中の make herself something to do（make O1 O2）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。これは try の目的語の中身。tried to make ~ で、目的語の不定詞1つの第3文型。
explanation: try to do で不定詞が目的語、後半 followed her も SVO。SVO。
author: William Dean Howells
authorJa: W・D・ハウエルズ
workJa: サイラス・ラパムの出世

text: I had expected to see him in the boardroom, on the Monday evening of which I am now writing, and had proposed to tell him, when we met, of dear Aunt Verinder’s arrival in London.
translation: 私が今こうして書いている月曜の晩には、理事会の部屋で彼に会えると思っていたので、会ったら、ヴェリンダー叔母さまがロンドンにお着きになったことを話すつもりでいた。
parts: in the boardroom, on the Monday evening of which I am now writing
to tell him, when we met, of dear Aunt Verinder’s arrival in London
point: to tell him ... of dear Aunt ~ の tell him（SVO＋of）や挿入の when we met に気を取られやすい。また to see him を目的の不定詞と見る誤りもある。expect / propose の目的語が不定詞の第3文型。
explanation: expect to do と propose to do。不定詞が目的語の SVO。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: How long this might have gone on I do not know, for they seemed to have no sense of time: but at last the captain of the ship, who seemed near beside himself (and no great wonder) in the midst of this crying and confusion, came to the side and begged us to depart.
target: How long this might have gone on I do not know
translation: これがどれほど長く続いたかもしれないのか、私にはわからない。彼らには時間の感覚がまったくないようだったからだ。だがついに、この泣き声と混乱のさなかで（それも無理はないが）ほとんど我を失っているように見えた船長が舷側にやってきて、私たちに立ち去るよう頼んだ。
parts: How long this might have gone on
point: 文頭の How long this might have gone on を主語や疑問文と見て、構造を見失いやすい。これは know の目的語が前に出た間接疑問。I do not know ~ で第3文型。
explanation: 目的語（間接疑問）が前に出た O-S-V の語順。SVO。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン
workJa: さらわれたデービッド

text: Thereupon, the man of the house, who had hitherto pretended to have no English, and driven me from his door by signals, suddenly began to speak as clearly as was needful, and agreed for five shillings to give me a night’s lodging and guide me the next day to Torosay.
translation: すると、それまで英語がわからないふりをして身ぶりで私を戸口から追い払っていたその家の主人が、急に必要なだけはっきりと話しはじめ、五シリングで一晩の宿を貸し、翌日トロセーまで案内することを承知した。
parts: who had hitherto pretended to have no English, and driven me from his door by signals
to give me a night’s lodging and guide me the next day to Torosay
point: 関係詞節の pretended to have no English, and driven me ~ や、agreed to give me a night's lodging（SVOO）に引っぱられて第4文型を選びやすい。begin / agree の目的語が不定詞の第3文型。
explanation: begin to speak と agree to give ...。不定詞が目的語の SVO。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン
workJa: さらわれたデービッド

text: That elder portion of the company which loved eating and drinking put on a look to signify that till this moment they had quite forgotten that it was customary to expect suppers on these occasions; going even further than this politeness of feature, and starting irrelevant subjects, the exceeding flatness and forced tone of which rather betrayed their object.
translation: 一座のうち飲み食いの好きな年長の者たちは、こういうときに夜食が出るのが習いだということを今の今まですっかり忘れていた、という顔をしてみせた。それどころか、この顔つきの礼儀を超えて、関係のない話題を持ち出しさえしたが、その話のひどく平板で無理のある調子が、かえってねらいを明かしてしまっていた。
parts: That elder portion of the company

to signify that till this moment they had quite forgotten that it was customary to expect suppers on these occasions; going even further than this politeness of feature, and starting irrelevant subjects, the exceeding flatness and forced tone of which rather betrayed their object
point: put on は「着る」の印象が強く、a look の扱いに迷いやすい。また to signify that ~ や it was customary to expect ~、of which 節にも気を取られる。put on a look（〜な顔をする）で第3文型。
explanation: put on「（表情を）浮かべる」の目的語が a look。SVO。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: A political pamphleteer had produced a few dozen pages, which he called "Who are John Hiram's heirs?" intending to give an infallible rule for the governance of all such establishments; and, at last, a member of the government promised that in the next session a short bill should be introduced for regulating the affairs of Barchester and other kindred concerns.
translation: ある政治パンフレット書きが「ジョン・ハイラムの相続人はだれか？」と題する数十ページを書き、そうした施設すべての運営について間違いのない規則を示そうとした。そしてついに政府の一員が、次の会期でバーチェスターなど同類の施設の運営を定める短い法案を提出させると約束した。
parts: which he called "Who are John Hiram's heirs?" intending to give an infallible rule for the governance of all such establishments
that in the next session a short bill should be introduced for regulating the affairs of Barchester and other kindred concerns
point: 関係詞節の which he called "..."（SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。また intending to give an infallible rule にもつられる。had produced pages / promised that ~ で第3文型。
explanation: produced pages と promised that 節。目的語をとる SVO が2つ。
author: Anthony Trollope
authorJa: アントニー・トロロープ

text: In the warm, breathless night air he heard a murmuring sound, perfectly inarticulate, as low as the sound of water coming from a spring, where there is no fall, and where there are no stones to fret it.
translation: 暖かくよどんだ夜気の中で、彼はつぶやくような音を聞いた。まったく言葉にならず、落ちる所もなく、それを波立たせる石もない泉からわき出る水の音のように低い音だった。
parts: In the warm, breathless night air
perfectly inarticulate, as low as the sound of water coming from a spring, where there is no fall, and where there are no stones to fret it
point: murmuring を動詞の進行形と見たり、where there are no stones to fret it の fret it（SVO）を判定したりしやすい。murmuring は sound を修飾する分詞。heard a sound で第3文型。
explanation: hear の目的語が sound。知覚動詞だが補語はないので SVO。
author: Willa Cather
authorJa: ウィラ・キャザー

text: Only a wall divided him from those happy young contemporaries of his with whom he shared a common mental life; men who had nothing to do from morning till night but to read, mark, learn, and inwardly digest.
translation: 自分と知的な生活を共にする同じ年ごろの幸せな若者たちから彼を隔てているのは、壁一枚だけだった。彼らは朝から晩まで、読み、心に留め、学び、内に消化すること以外に何もすることのない者たちだった。
parts: from those happy young contemporaries of his with whom he shared a common mental life; men who had nothing to do from morning till night but to read, mark, learn, and inwardly digest
point: divide は「分かれる」の自動詞にもなり、また from his contemporaries ~ を2つ目の要素と見て第5文型を選びやすい。with whom ~ / men who had nothing to do ~ も修飾語。divided him で第3文型。
explanation: divide O from 〜「O を〜から隔てる」。divide の目的語が him。SVO。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: Seth, always timid in his behaviour towards his mother, from the sense that he had no influence over her, felt it was useless to attempt to persuade or soothe her till this passion was past; so he contented himself with tending the back kitchen fire and folding up his father’s clothes, which had been hanging out to dry since morning—afraid to move about in the room where his mother was, lest he should irritate her further.
target: Seth, always timid in his behaviour towards his mother, from the sense that he had no influence over her, felt it was useless to attempt to persuade or soothe her till this passion was past
translation: セスはいつも母に対しては臆病だった。自分には母を動かす力がないと感じていたからだ。それで、この激情がおさまるまでは、母を説き伏せたりなだめたりしようとしても無駄だと感じ、裏の台所の火の世話をしたり、朝から干してあった父の服をたたんだりするだけにしておいた。母のいる部屋で動き回ると、もっと苛立たせはしないかと恐れたのだ。
parts: always timid in his behaviour towards his mother, from the sense that he had no influence over her
it was useless to attempt to persuade or soothe her till this passion was past
point: that が省略されているので、it was useless to attempt ~ を別の文と見て第2文型を選びやすい。また feel は「〜と感じる」の第2文型にもなる。省略された that 節が felt の目的語。第3文型。
explanation: feel の目的語が (that) it was useless ... の節。判定部分は SVO。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: As they drove from Waterloo to Chelsea, Katharine began to have some compunction about her father, which, together with the opening of offices and the need of working in them on Monday, made it difficult to plan another festival for the following day.
translation: ウォータールーからチェルシーへ車で向かううち、キャサリンは父のことで少し気がとがめはじめた。そのうえ月曜には事務所が開き、そこで働かねばならないこともあって、翌日にまた催しを計画するのは難しくなった。
parts: As they drove from Waterloo to Chelsea
about her father, which, together with the opening of offices and the need of working in them on Monday, made it difficult to plan another festival for the following day
point: 関係詞節の中の made it difficult to plan ~（形式目的語の SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これは compunction を修飾する部分。begin の目的語は to have ~ の不定詞。第3文型。
explanation: begin to do で不定詞が目的語。SVO。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: Winterbourne wondered whether she was seriously wounded, and for a moment almost wished that her sense of injury might be such as to make it becoming in him to attempt to reassure and comfort her.
translation: ウィンターボーンは、彼女がひどく傷ついたのだろうかと思い、一瞬、彼女の傷ついた気持ちが、自分が慰め、元気づけようとするのがふさわしいほどのものであってほしい、とさえ思いかけた。
parts: and for a moment almost wished
that her sense of injury might be such as to make it becoming in him to attempt to reassure and comfort her
point: wished の that 節の中の such as to make it becoming in him to attempt ~（形式目的語の SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これは目的語の中身。wondered whether ~ / wished that ~ で第3文型。
explanation: wonder whether 節、wish that 節。名詞節が目的語の SVO。
author: Henry James
authorJa: ヘンリー・ジェイムズ

text: On the morning you left Marygreen, when your goods were on the waggon, you wished me good-bye, and said your scheme was to be a university man and enter the Church—that a degree was the necessary hall-mark of one who wanted to do anything as a theologian or teacher.”
target: you wished me good-bye
translation: あなたがメアリーグリーンを出ていった朝、荷物が荷馬車に積まれていたとき、あなたは私に別れを告げて、大学の人間になって教会に入るのが計画だと言ったわね――学位は、神学者や教師として何かしたい者に必要な折り紙なのだと。
point: wish は「望む」の印象が強く、me good-bye を「私が〜であることを望む」と読み違えて第5文型を選びやすい。wish 人 good-bye は「人に別れを告げる」で、目的語2つの第4文型。
explanation: wish O1 O2「O1 に O2 を述べる」。me と good-bye の2つの目的語をとる SVOO。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: His wife had not the slightest reason to feel that anything would ever go amiss with their household, and yet the shadows which run before gave her a thought of the good of it now and then.
target: the shadows which run before gave her a thought of the good of it now and then
translation: 妻には、自分たちの家庭で何かがうまくいかなくなると思う理由はこれっぽっちもなかった。それでも、先立って走る影が、ときおり今の暮らしのありがたさを思わせた。
parts: a thought of the good of it
point: 主語の shadows which run before（比喩）が無生物で「影が彼女に考えを与えた」と読みにくい。また後半の reason to feel that ~ にもつられる。gave her a thought で、her と a thought の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: give O1 O2「O1 に O2 を与える」。her と a thought が目的語の SVOO。
author: Theodore Dreiser
authorJa: セオドア・ドライサー

text: These two tricks of his--of crumpling up the eyelids, so as to concentrate the power of sight, which made him look stern and thoughtful; and the odd twitching of the lips that was preliminary to a smile, which made him look intensely merry--gave the varying expressions of his face a greater range "from grave to gay, from lively to severe," than is common with most men.
translation: 彼のこの二つの癖――視力を集めるようにまぶたをすぼめる癖は彼をいかめしく考え深げに見せ、笑いの前ぶれに唇がおかしな具合にぴくつく癖は彼をひどく陽気に見せた――が、移り変わる彼の表情に、たいていの人よりも広い「厳から陽へ、快から厳へ」の幅を与えていた。
parts: of crumpling up the eyelids, so as to concentrate the power of sight, which made him look stern and thoughtful; and the odd twitching of the lips that was preliminary to a smile, which made him look intensely merry
the varying expressions of his face
a greater range "from grave to gay, from lively to severe," than is common with most men
point: ダッシュの間の which made him look stern ~（使役の SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これは tricks の中身。gave the expressions a greater range で、expressions と range の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: give O1 O2 で、O1 は expressions、O2 は a greater range。SVOO。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: They were proud of him, and Bromfield Corey, who found a delicate, aesthetic pleasure in the heroism with which Lapham had withstood Rogers and his temptations--something finely dramatic and unconsciously effective,--wrote him a letter which would once have flattered the rough soul almost to ecstasy, though now he affected to slight it in showing it.
target: Bromfield Corey, who found a delicate, aesthetic pleasure in the heroism with which Lapham had withstood Rogers and his temptations--something finely dramatic and unconsciously effective,--wrote him a letter which would once have flattered the rough soul almost to ecstasy, though now he affected to slight it in showing it
translation: 人々は彼を誇りに思った。ロジャーズとその誘惑に耐え抜いたラパムの英雄ぶりに――何か見事に劇的で、それと知らずに効果的なものに――繊細で美的な喜びを見いだしたブロムフィールド・コーリーは、彼に手紙を書いた。それは以前なら、その粗野な魂を有頂天にさせるほどうれしがらせたはずのものだったが、いまの彼はそれを人に見せながら、気にもしていないふりをした。
parts: who found a delicate, aesthetic pleasure in the heroism with which Lapham had withstood Rogers and his temptations--something finely dramatic and unconsciously effective
which would once have flattered the rough soul almost to ecstasy, though now he affected to slight it in showing it
point: 挿入の who found a delicate pleasure in the heroism with which ~ が長く、動詞を見失いやすい。また write は「〜を書く」で目的語1つの第3文型を選びやすい。wrote him a letter で、him と letter の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: write O1 O2「O1 に O2 を書き送る」。SVOO。
author: William Dean Howells
authorJa: W・D・ハウエルズ
workJa: サイラス・ラパムの出世

text: When her husband came in she told him her solution of the bird-cage mystery; and begged Donald to help her in finding out, as soon as possible, whither Henchard had banished himself, that she might make her peace with him; try to do something to render his life less that of an outcast, and more tolerable to him.
target: she told him her solution of the bird-cage mystery
translation: 夫が入ってくると、彼女は鳥かごの謎の答えを話し、ヘンチャードがどこへ身を引いたのかをできるだけ早く探す手伝いをしてほしいとドナルドに頼んだ。彼と仲直りし、彼の暮らしがのけ者らしさを少しでも減らし、もっと耐えやすくなるよう何かしてやりたかったのだ。
parts: her solution of the bird-cage mystery
point: 後半の begged Donald to help her（beg O to do、SVOC）や render his life less ~（SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。主節は she told him her solution で、him と solution の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: tell O1 O2「O1 に O2 を話す」。判定部分は SVOO（後半 begged Donald to help は SVOC）。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: カスターブリッジの市長

text: I offered him a share, as was much the custom in those days; but he was far too great a man to sit with such poor customers as Ransome and myself, and he was leaving the room, when I called him back to ask if he knew Mr. Rankeillor.
target: I offered him a share, as was much the custom in those days
translation: 当時のならいどおり、私は彼にも一杯どうかとすすめた。だが彼はランサムや私のような貧しい客と同席するにはあまりに偉い人物で、部屋を出ていこうとしたので、私は呼び戻してランケイラー氏を知っているかと尋ねた。
parts: as was much the custom in those days
point: as was much the custom（as は関係代名詞的）や too great a man to sit ~、ask if ~ に気を取られやすい。offer は「〜を申し出る」で目的語1つにも見える。offered him a share で、him と share の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: offer O1 O2「O1 に O2 を差し出す」。SVOO。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン
workJa: さらわれたデービッド

text: He gravely taught them the letters on the backs of the encyclopedias, and when polite visitors asked about the mental progress of the “little ones,” they were horrified to hear the children earnestly repeating A-And, And-Aus, Aus-Bis, Bis-Cal, Cal-Cha.
target: He gravely taught them the letters on the backs of the encyclopedias
translation: 彼はまじめな顔で子どもたちに百科事典の背の文字を教えこんだ。それで、礼儀正しい客が「おちびさんたち」の知恵のつき具合を尋ねると、子どもたちが熱心に「A から And、And から Aus、Aus から Bis、Bis から Cal、Cal から Cha」と唱えるのを聞いてぎょっとするのだった。
parts: the letters on the backs of the encyclopedias
point: 後半の were horrified to hear the children repeating ~（知覚動詞の SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。また taught を「教えた」で目的語1つと見る誤りもある。taught them the letters で第4文型。
explanation: teach O1 O2「O1 に O2 を教える」。SVOO。
author: Sinclair Lewis
authorJa: シンクレア・ルイス

text: He told them that the house of theirs to which he alluded was this their church, in which he now addressed them for the first time; that their most welcome and proper manner of bidding him God-speed would be their patient obedience to his teaching of the gospel; but that he could put forward no claim to such conduct on their part unless he taught them the great Christian doctrine of works and faith combined.
translation: 彼は人々に言った。自分が言及したあなたがたの家とは、自分がいま初めて語りかけているこの教会のことであり、自分の門出をいちばん喜ばしく正しく祝ってくれるのは、自分の説く福音にあなたがたが辛抱強く従うことである。だが、行いと信仰を合わせた偉大なキリスト教の教えを説かないかぎり、そうしたふるまいを求める資格は自分にはない、と。
parts: that the house of theirs to which he alluded was this their church, in which he now addressed them for the first time; that their most welcome and proper manner of bidding him God-speed would be their patient obedience to his teaching of the gospel; but that he could put forward no claim to such conduct on their part unless he taught them the great Christian doctrine of works and faith combined
point: that 節が3つ並び、その中の manner of bidding him God-speed（bid O O）や taught them the doctrine に気を取られて、目的語の範囲を見失いやすい。told them that ~ で、them と that 節が目的語。第4文型。
explanation: tell O that 節「O に〜と言う」。that 節を2つ目の目的語とみる SVOO。
note: 学校文法では tell O that 節を SVOO とする。that 節を目的語と区別して副詞的にみる説明もある。
author: Anthony Trollope
authorJa: アントニー・トロロープ

text: The bones of King Edward “the Martyr,” carefully removed hither for holy preservation, brought Shaston a renown which made it the resort of pilgrims from every part of Europe, and enabled it to maintain a reputation extending far beyond English shores.
translation: 聖なる保存のため丁重にここへ移された「殉教王」エドワードの遺骨は、シャストンに名声をもたらした。その名声によって町はヨーロッパ中から巡礼の訪れる地となり、英国の岸辺をはるかに越えて広がる評判を保つことができた。
parts: The bones of King Edward “the Martyr,”
carefully removed hither for holy preservation
which made it the resort of pilgrims from every part of Europe, and enabled it to maintain a reputation extending far beyond English shores
point: 主語の bones の後ろの removed hither や、関係詞節の made it the resort（SVOC）、enabled it to maintain（SVOC）に引っぱられて第5文型を選びやすい。brought Shaston a renown で第4文型。
explanation: bring O1 O2「O1 に O2 をもたらす」。SVOO。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: The boy handed him a letter, merely mentioning that he had been entrusted with it by an old lady whom he did not know, and who had given him no instructions to wait for an answer.
translation: 少年は彼に一通の手紙を手渡した。そして、知らない老婦人に預けられたもので、返事を待つようにとは何も言われていない、とだけ言い添えた。
parts: merely mentioning that he had been entrusted with it by an old lady whom he did not know, and who had given him no instructions to wait for an answer
point: 後半の who had given him no instructions to wait（SVOO）や merely mentioning that ~ に気を取られやすい。hand を「手」と読む誤りもある。handed him a letter で、him と letter の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: hand O1 O2「O1 に O2 を手渡す」。SVOO。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: When his father came down, rubbing his long hands together, and looking aloof from all the cares of the practical world, in an artistic withdrawal, from which his eye ranged over the breakfast-table before he sat down, Mrs. Corey told him what she and their son had been saying.
translation: 父親が長い手をこすりあわせながら、実際の世の中のわずらわしさにはまるで関わりのない、芸術家らしい超然とした顔で下りてきて、腰を下ろす前に朝食のテーブルにさっと目を走らせると、コーリー夫人は、自分と息子が話していたことを彼に聞かせた。
parts: When his father came down, rubbing his long hands together, and looking aloof from all the cares of the practical world, in an artistic withdrawal, from which his eye ranged over the breakfast-table before he sat down
what she and their son had been saying
point: rubbing ... and looking aloof の分詞構文や from which his eye ranged over ~ に気を取られやすい。また what 節を独立した文と見る誤りもある。told him what ~ で、him と what 節の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: tell O1 O2 で、O2 は what 節。SVOO。
author: William Dean Howells
authorJa: W・D・ハウエルズ
workJa: サイラス・ラパムの出世

text: And even while this thought was crossing my mind, as I stood leaning quiet and solitary against the ship’s side, she came tripping up to me, an utter stranger, with a camp-stool in her hand, and smiling a smile of which the levity puzzled and startled me, though it showed a perfect set of perfect teeth, she offered me the accommodation of this piece of furniture.
target: smiling a smile of which the levity puzzled and startled me, though it showed a perfect set of perfect teeth, she offered me the accommodation of this piece of furniture
translation: そして私がひとり静かに船べりにもたれ、そんなことを考えているあいだにも、彼女は折りたたみ椅子を手に、見ず知らずの私のところへ軽やかにやってきた。見事にそろった見事な歯がのぞいていたとはいえ、その軽薄さに私が戸惑い、ぎょっとさせられるような笑みを浮かべて、彼女はこの家具を使ってはどうかとすすめた。
parts: smiling a smile of which the levity puzzled and startled me, though it showed a perfect set of perfect teeth
the accommodation of this piece of furniture
point: 文頭の smiling a smile of which the levity puzzled and startled me（SVO）に引っぱられて第3文型を選びやすい。これは付帯状況の分詞構文。offered me the accommodation で、me と accommodation の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: offer O1 O2「O1 に O2 を差し出す」。SVOO。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: I had some work to do which pressed, so I told him that if he would go alone I would be glad, as then I should not have to keep him waiting; so I called an attendant and gave him the necessary instructions.
target: I told him that if he would go alone I would be glad, as then I should not have to keep him waiting
translation: 急ぎの仕事があったので、一人で行ってくれたらありがたい、そうすれば待たせずにすむから、と彼に言った。そして付き添いを呼んで必要な指示を出した。
parts: that if he would go alone I would be glad, as then I should not have to keep him waiting
point: that 節の中の keep him waiting（keep O -ing、SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。これは目的語の中の理由の節。told him that ~ で、him と that 節の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: tell O that 節で SVOO。
author: Bram Stoker
authorJa: ブラム・ストーカー

text: He handed her a great bundle of newspaper cuttings, and, begging her to give him her views upon the yellow leaflet before lunch-time, he turned with alacrity to his different sheets of paper and his different bottles of ink.
target: He handed her a great bundle of newspaper cuttings
translation: 彼は彼女に新聞の切り抜きの大きな束を手渡し、昼までに黄色いビラについて意見を聞かせてほしいと頼むと、さっさと向き直って、いろいろな紙といろいろなインク壺に取りかかった。
parts: a great bundle of newspaper cuttings
point: 後半の begging her to give him her views（beg O to do の中に SVOO）が目立ち、第5文型を選びやすい。これは付帯状況の分詞構文。handed her a bundle で、her と bundle の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: hand O1 O2「O1 に O2 を手渡す」。SVOO。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: Mr. Thorne gave him a look which undeaned him completely for the moment, but he soon remembered his high hopes and, recovering himself quickly, sustained his probable coming dignity by a laugh at Mr. Thorne's expense.
target: Mr. Thorne gave him a look which undeaned him completely
translation: ソーン氏が彼に向けた視線は、一瞬、彼から主任司祭の気分をすっかり奪い去った。だが彼はすぐに自分の大きな望みを思い出し、急いで気を取り直すと、ソーン氏をだしにして笑い、いずれ手にするはずの威厳を保った。
point: 関係詞節の which undeaned him completely（造語の他動詞）や recovering himself quickly に気を取られやすい。gave him a look（彼をにらんだ）で、him と look の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: give O1 O2 で、him と a look が目的語。SVOO。
author: Anthony Trollope
authorJa: アントニー・トロロープ

text: His experience in such matters told him that Rosanna was in all probability carrying about her a memorandum of the hiding-place, to guide her, in case she returned to it, under changed circumstances and after a lapse of time.
translation: こうしたことについての経験から、彼にはわかった。ロザンナはおそらく隠し場所の覚え書きを身につけていて、事情が変わって、しばらくたってからそこへ戻る場合の手がかりにしているのだ、と。
parts: that Rosanna was in all probability carrying about her a memorandum of the hiding-place, to guide her, in case she returned to it, under changed circumstances and after a lapse of time
point: that 節の中の was carrying about her a memorandum（目的語が長いため about her が前に出た形）に気を取られやすい。主語も無生物で読みにくい。told him that ~ で、him と that 節の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: 物が主語の tell O that 節「経験が彼に〜と教えた」。SVOO。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: It gave her a goal certainly, but the fact of having a goal led her to dwell exclusively upon her obsession; so that when she rang the bell of Mary’s flat, she did not for a moment consider how this demand would strike Mary.
target: It gave her a goal certainly
translation: それはたしかに彼女に目標を与えた。だが目標を持ったことで、彼女はその思いこみばかりに気を取られるようになった。それでメアリーの部屋の呼び鈴を鳴らしたときも、この頼みがメアリーにどう受け取られるか、一瞬たりとも考えなかった。
point: 後半の led her to dwell exclusively upon ~（lead O to do、SVOC）が目立つので、第5文型を選びやすい。また certainly を目的語の一部と見る誤りもある。gave her a goal で第4文型。
explanation: give O1 O2 で SVOO。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: Its many and growing commercial opportunities gave it widespread fame, which made of it a giant magnet, drawing to itself, from all quarters, the hopeful and the hopeless—those who had their fortune yet to make and those whose fortunes and affairs had reached a disastrous climax elsewhere.
translation: 数多く、しかも増え続ける商売の機会が、その町に広い名声を与えた。その名声が町を巨大な磁石にし、四方八方から望みを抱く者も望みを失った者も引き寄せた――これから運を開こうとする者も、よその土地で運も仕事も破滅のどん底に至った者も。
parts: Its many and growing commercial opportunities

which made of it a giant magnet, drawing to itself, from all quarters, the hopeful and the hopeless—those who had their fortune yet to make and those whose fortunes and affairs had reached a disastrous climax elsewhere
point: 関係詞節の made of it a giant magnet（make O C の of it が前に出た形）が目立ち、第5文型を選びやすい。drawing to itself ~ も紛らわしい。gave it widespread fame で、it と fame の2つが目的語。第4文型。
explanation: give O1 O2 で、it（=the city）と fame が目的語。SVOO。
author: Theodore Dreiser
authorJa: セオドア・ドライサー

text: Nobody should find out how miserable she was, nobody should know she was disappointed about anything; and the thought that the eyes of her aunt and uncle would be upon her gave her the self-command which often accompanies a great dread.
target: the thought that the eyes of her aunt and uncle would be upon her gave her the self-command which often accompanies a great dread
translation: 自分がどれほどみじめか、だれにも見破られてはならない、何かにがっかりしているなどと、だれにも知られてはならない。そして伯母と伯父の目が自分に注がれるだろうという思いが、大きな恐れにしばしば伴う、あの自制心を彼女に与えた。
parts: that the eyes of her aunt and uncle would be upon her
the self-command which often accompanies a great dread
point: 主語 the thought の後ろの同格の that 節（would be upon her）が長く、動詞を見失いやすい。また前半の find out how miserable she was にもつられる。gave her the self-command で第4文型。
explanation: give O1 O2「O1 に O2 を与える」。SVOO。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: His happy love—the knowledge that his steps were carrying him nearer and nearer to Hetty, who was so soon to be his—was to his thoughts what the sweet morning air was to his sensations: it gave him a consciousness of well-being that made activity delightful.
target: it gave him a consciousness of well-being that made activity delightful
translation: 幸せな恋――自分の足がヘティに、もうすぐ自分のものになるヘティに、一歩ごとに近づいているのだという思い――は、さわやかな朝の空気が彼の感覚にとってそうであるものが、彼の考えにとってそうであるものだった。それは彼に満ち足りた気分を与え、体を動かすことを楽しいものにした。
parts: a consciousness of well-being that made activity delightful
point: 前半の A is to B what C is to D の構文や、a consciousness of well-being that made activity delightful（SVOC）に引っぱられて、第5文型を選びやすい。gave him a consciousness で第4文型。
explanation: give O1 O2 で、him と consciousness が目的語。SVOO。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: Indeed, sometimes, when the door by which she used to enter was opened by any chance, Molly caught herself looking round as if she expected to see the tall, languid figure in the elegant draperies of rich silk and soft lace, which Mrs. Hamley was wont to wear of an evening.
translation: 実際、ときどき、ハムリー夫人がいつも入ってきていた戸口の扉が何かの拍子に開くと、モリーは、夫人が夕方によくまとっていた豪華な絹と柔らかなレースの優雅な衣装の、背の高い、もの憂げな姿が見えるのを期待しているかのように、思わず振り返っている自分に気づくのだった。
parts: Indeed, sometimes, when the door by which she used to enter was opened by any chance
as if she expected to see the tall, languid figure in the elegant draperies of rich silk and soft lace, which Mrs. Hamley was wont to wear of an evening
point: catch は「捕まえる」の印象が強く、looking round を修飾語と見て第3文型を選びやすい。また as if she expected to see ~ にもつられる。catch oneself -ing（ふと〜しているのに気づく）で、herself＝looking。第5文型。
explanation: catch O -ing「O が〜しているのに気づく」。herself と looking round が O と C。SVOC。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: One day, at a quiet early hour, I found myself nearly alone in a certain gallery, wherein one particular picture of portentous size, set up in the best light, having a cordon of protection stretched before it, and a cushioned bench duly set in front for the accommodation of worshipping connoisseurs, who, having gazed themselves off their feet, might be fain to complete the business sitting: this picture, I say, seemed to consider itself the queen of the collection.
target: I found myself nearly alone in a certain gallery
translation: ある日、静かな朝早い時刻に、私はある画廊にほとんど一人きりでいた。そこでは、とてつもなく大きな一枚の絵がいちばんよい光の中に掲げられ、前には保護の綱が張られ、さらにその前には、ひれ伏して眺める目利きたちのために、ちゃんとクッションつきの長椅子が置かれていた。目利きたちは見とれすぎて足が立たなくなると、座って仕上げをしたくなるかもしれないからだ。この絵は、いわば自分がこの所蔵品の女王だと思っているようだった。
point: nearly alone を「ひとりで」という修飾語と見て、第3文型を選びやすい。また後半の consider itself the queen（SVOC）も紛らわしい。find oneself C で、myself＝alone。第5文型。
explanation: find oneself C「気がつくと〜の状態にいる」。myself と nearly alone が O と C。SVOC。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: “As if I had not something better to do!” rejoined he; but I saw him give her a piece of gold, which she took unscrupulously, and then danced off to answer the door-bell, ringing just now every five minutes, as the various servants came to fetch the half-boarders.
target: I saw him give her a piece of gold, which she took unscrupulously
translation: 「ほかにもっとましなすることがないとでも言うのか！」と彼は言い返した。けれども私は、彼が彼女に金貨を一枚渡すのを見た。彼女は遠慮なくそれを受け取り、それから玄関の呼び鈴に出ようと踊るように駆けていった。半寄宿生を迎えに来るさまざまな召使いたちのせいで、呼び鈴はちょうど五分おきに鳴っていた。
parts: give her a piece of gold
point: give her a piece of gold（SVOO）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。これは知覚動詞の後ろの原形部分。see＋O＋原形で、him が give する関係。第5文型。
explanation: see O 原形「O が〜するのを見る」。補語の中に give her a piece of gold（give O O）が入っている。SVOC。
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorJa: シャーロット・ブロンテ

text: Her father's depression, which was still continuing and rendering him very silent, made her uneasy; yet she wished to conceal it from Mr. Preston; and so she talked away, trying to obviate the sort of personal bearing which their host would give to everything.
target: Her father's depression, which was still continuing and rendering him very silent, made her uneasy
translation: 父の落ちこみはまだ続いていて、父をひどく無口にしていたので、彼女は不安になった。それでもプレストン氏にはそれを隠したかった。だから彼女はしゃべり続け、主人役が何でも個人的なことに結びつけてしまうような話の向きを避けようとした。
parts: which was still continuing and rendering him very silent
point: 関係詞節の rendering him very silent（render O C）や、後半の the bearing which their host would give to ~ に気を取られやすい。主節は made her uneasy で、her＝uneasy の第5文型。
explanation: make O C「O を C にする」。her と uneasy が O と C。SVOC。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: Yet something within him made him wince, as if his duties were not rightly performed, when, as the cloth was drawn, the two awkward lads rose up with joyful alacrity, gave him a nod, which was to be interpreted as a bow, knocked against each other in their endeavours to get out of the dining-room quickly; and then might be heard dashing along a passage which led to the surgery, choking with half-suppressed laughter.
target: Yet something within him made him wince, as if his duties were not rightly performed
translation: それでも、テーブルクロスが片づけられるやいなや、ぶきっちょな二人の若者がうれしそうにさっと立ち上がり、お辞儀のつもりらしいうなずきをして、急いで食堂を出ようとしてぶつかりあい、やがて半ば押し殺した笑いにむせながら診療室へ続く廊下を駆けていくのが聞こえてくると、彼の内なる何かが、まるで自分の務めが正しく果たされていないかのように、彼をたじろがせた。
parts: as if his duties were not rightly performed
point: wince を名詞や修飾語と見て、him だけを目的語とする第3文型を選びやすい。また when 節の中の関係詞節や choking with ~ も長い。使役の make＋O＋原形で、him が wince する関係。第5文型。
explanation: make O 原形「O に〜させる」。him と wince が O と C。SVOC。
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
authorJa: エリザベス・ギャスケル

text: Moreover the guests did not think it anything amiss when Mr. Plomacy, rising to say grace, prayed that God would make them all truly thankful for the good things which Madame Thorne in her great liberality had set before them!
translation: そのうえ客たちは、プロマシー氏が食前の祈りに立ち、ソーン夫人がたいへん気前よく自分たちの前に並べてくれたごちそうに、神が自分たち皆を心から感謝させてくださいますように、と祈ったときも、それを少しもおかしなことだと思わなかった。
parts: when Mr. Plomacy, rising to say grace, prayed that God would make them all truly thankful for the good things which Madame Thorne in her great liberality had set before them
point: think は that 節をとる第3文型の印象が強く、後半の prayed that God would make them all truly thankful（SVOC）にも気を取られやすい。think O C（O を C だと思う）で、it＝anything amiss。第5文型。
explanation: think O C「O を C だと思う」。it と anything amiss が O と C。SVOC。
note: it は後ろの when 節の状況を指す。仮目的語とみる説明もあるが、いずれにしても SVOC。
author: Anthony Trollope
authorJa: アントニー・トロロープ

text: The interest I felt in this strange man had impelled me, in the first instance, to give him the opportunity of speaking to me; reserving what I might have to say, on my side, in relation to his employer, until I was first satisfied that he was a person in whose delicacy and discretion I could trust.
translation: この奇妙な男に抱いた関心に駆られて、私はまず彼に、私に話しかける機会を与えることにした。その雇い主について自分の側から言うかもしれないことは、彼が繊細さと分別を信頼できる人物だと確かめるまで、取っておくことにして。
parts: I felt in this strange man
to give him the opportunity of speaking to me
reserving what I might have to say, on my side, in relation to his employer, until I was first satisfied that he was a person in whose delicacy and discretion I could trust
point: 補語の不定詞の中の give him the opportunity（SVOO）が目立つので、第4文型を選びやすい。また in whose delicacy I could trust も紛らわしい。impel O to do（O を〜する気にさせる）で、me が give する関係。第5文型。
explanation: impel O to do「O を駆り立てて〜させる」。me と to give ... が O と C。SVOC。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: But standing near the old oak frame which holds our large looking-glass, I saw her reflected in it, slyly slipping the locket which Mr. Franklin had given to her, out of the bosom of her dress, and showing it to him for a moment, with a smile which certainly meant something out of the common, before she tripped off to bed.
target: I saw her reflected in it, slyly slipping the locket which Mr. Franklin had given to her, out of the bosom of her dress, and showing it to him for a moment, with a smile which certainly meant something out of the common, before she tripped off to bed
translation: しかし大きな姿見をはめた古い樫の枠の近くに立っていた私は、鏡に彼女が映っているのを見た。フランクリンさまから贈られたロケットを服の胸元からこっそり取り出し、たしかにただならぬ意味のこもった笑みを浮かべて一瞬それを彼に見せ、それから軽い足取りで寝室に引き上げていくところだった。
parts: slyly slipping the locket which Mr. Franklin had given to her, out of the bosom of her dress, and showing it to him for a moment, with a smile which certainly meant something out of the common, before she tripped off to bed
point: reflected を受動態の動詞と見たり、slyly slipping the locket（SVO）を判定したりしやすい。知覚動詞 see＋O＋過去分詞（reflected）と＋-ing（slipping）が並び、her＝reflected / slipping の関係。第5文型。
explanation: see O 過去分詞／-ing。her に reflected in it と slipping ... and showing ... が補語として続く。SVOC。
author: Wilkie Collins
authorJa: ウィルキー・コリンズ

text: When she dared to go shopping in her new checked suit with the black-embroidered sulphur collar, she had as good as invited all of Gopher Prairie (which interested itself in nothing so intimately as in new clothes and the cost thereof) to investigate her.
translation: 黒い刺繍のある硫黄色の襟がついた新しいチェックのスーツで思い切って買い物に出たとき、彼女はゴーファー・プレーリーの町じゅう（新しい服とその値段ほど身近に関心を寄せるものはない町だった）に、自分を詮索してくれと招いたも同然だった。
parts: When she dared to go shopping in her new checked suit with the black-embroidered sulphur collar
(which interested itself in nothing so intimately as in new clothes and the cost thereof)
point: as good as（〜も同然）を比較の構文と見て構造を見失いやすい。またカッコ内の nothing so 〜 as ... にもつられる。invite O to do（O に〜するよう誘う）で、Gopher Prairie が investigate する関係。第5文型。
explanation: invite O to do「O に〜するよう誘う」。all of Gopher Prairie と to investigate her が O と C。SVOC。
author: Sinclair Lewis
authorJa: シンクレア・ルイス

text: She saw herself persuading children to read charming fairy tales, helping young men to find books on mechanics, being ever so courteous to old men who were hunting for newspapers--the light of the library, an authority on books, invited to dinners with poets and explorers, reading a paper to an association of distinguished scholars.
translation: 彼女は思い描いた。子どもたちにすてきなおとぎ話を読むよう勧め、若者たちが機械の本を探すのを手伝い、新聞を探しにくる老人たちにこの上なく親切にしている自分を――図書館の光、本の権威として、詩人や探検家と一緒に夕食に招かれ、著名な学者の会で論文を読み上げる自分を。
parts: persuading children to read charming fairy tales, helping young men to find books on mechanics, being ever so courteous to old men who were hunting for newspapers--the light of the library, an authority on books, invited to dinners with poets and explorers, reading a paper to an association of distinguished scholars
point: 補語の中の persuading children to read や helping young men to find（SVOC）が目立ち、それを判定しやすい。それらは herself の様子を表す補語。see oneself -ing で、herself＝persuading ~。第5文型。
explanation: see oneself -ing「自分が〜しているのを思い描く」。herself と -ing 形が O と C。SVOC。
author: Sinclair Lewis
authorJa: シンクレア・ルイス

text: True to her nature, she corresponded with Mrs. Vance as long as she still lived in Seventy-eighth Street, but when she was compelled to move into Thirteenth, her fear that the latter would take it as an indication of reduced circumstances caused her to study some way of avoiding the necessity of giving her address.
target: her fear that the latter would take it as an indication of reduced circumstances caused her to study some way of avoiding the necessity of giving her address
translation: いかにも彼女らしく、まだ七十八丁目に住んでいるあいだはヴァンス夫人と手紙をやりとりしていたが、十三丁目に移らざるをえなくなると、相手がそれを暮らし向きが悪くなったしるしと受け取るのではないかという心配から、住所を書かずにすむ方法をあれこれ考えるようになった。
parts: that the latter would take it as an indication of reduced circumstances
to study some way of avoiding the necessity of giving her address
point: 主語の後ろの同格の that 節（take it as an indication）が長く、動詞を見失いやすい。また avoiding や giving の動名詞にもつられる。cause O to do（O に〜させる）で、her が study する関係。第5文型。
explanation: cause O to do「O に〜させる」。her と to study ... が O と C。SVOC。
author: Theodore Dreiser
authorJa: セオドア・ドライサー

text: But when I had come so far a way already, mere shame would not suffer me to desist till I had put the matter to the touch of proof; I was bound, out of mere self-respect, to carry it through; and little as I liked the sound of what I heard, and slow as I began to travel, I still kept asking my way and still kept advancing.
target: mere shame would not suffer me to desist till I had put the matter to the touch of proof
translation: しかしここまで来てしまった以上、恥ずかしさだけでも、事を確かめるまではやめることを私に許さなかった。自尊心だけからでも、やり遂げねばならなかった。耳にすることはまったく気に入らず、足取りも重くなりはじめたが、それでも私は道を尋ね続け、進み続けた。
parts: till I had put the matter to the touch of proof
point: suffer を「苦しむ」と読むと、me to desist の扱いに困って第3文型を選びやすい。ここは「〜させる・許す」の意味。suffer O to do で、me が desist する関係。little as I liked ~ なども修飾語。第5文型。
explanation: suffer O to do「O が〜するのを許す」。me と to desist が O と C。SVOC。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン
workJa: さらわれたデービッド

text: I had no sooner seen these people coming than I made up my mind (for no reason that I can tell) to go through with my adventure; and when the first came alongside of me, I rose up from the bracken and asked him the way to Aucharn.
target: I had no sooner seen these people coming than I made up my mind (for no reason that I can tell) to go through with my adventure
translation: その人たちがやってくるのを見るやいなや、私は（なぜかは言えないが）この冒険をやり通そうと心を決めた。そして先頭の者がそばまで来ると、シダの茂みから立ち上がって、オーカーンへの道を尋ねた。
parts: than I made up my mind (for no reason that I can tell) to go through with my adventure
point: no sooner 〜 than ... の構文で、than 節の made up my mind to go ~ を判定しやすい。また coming を修飾語と見る誤りもある。知覚動詞 see＋O＋-ing で、these people が coming する関係。第5文型。
explanation: see O -ing「O が〜しているのを見る」。these people と coming が O と C。SVOC。
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorJa: ロバート・ルイス・スティーヴンソン
workJa: さらわれたデービッド

text: Jude had one day seen him selling a pot of coloured lard to an old woman as a certain cure for a bad leg, the woman arranging to pay a guinea, in instalments of a shilling a fortnight, for the precious salve, which, according to the physician, could only be obtained from a particular animal which grazed on Mount Sinai, and was to be captured only at great risk to life and limb.
translation: ジュードはある日、彼が色をつけたラードの壺を、脚の悪いのが必ず治る薬だと言って老婆に売っているのを見たことがあった。老婆は二週間ごとに一シリングずつの分割で一ギニーを払うことになっていた。その貴い軟膏は、医者の言うところでは、シナイ山で草を食むある特別な動物からしか取れず、その動物は命と手足を大いに危険にさらさなければ捕まえられないのだった。
parts: selling a pot of coloured lard

to an old woman as a certain cure for a bad leg, the woman arranging to pay a guinea, in instalments of a shilling a fortnight, for the precious salve, which, according to the physician, could only be obtained from a particular animal which grazed on Mount Sinai, and was to be captured only at great risk to life and limb
point: 独立分詞構文の the woman arranging to pay ~ や、salve を修飾する長い関係詞節に気を取られやすい。知覚動詞 see＋O＋-ing で、him が selling する関係。第5文型。
explanation: see O -ing「O が〜しているのを見る」。him と selling ... が O と C。SVOC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: Yes, in the fondness and foolishness of his young heart, after walking four miles, in a drizzling rain without overcoat or umbrella, and in face of a remark from his love that he was not to come because he would be tired, he had made it his business to wander this mile out of his way again, from sheer wish of spending ten minutes in her presence.
translation: そうなのだ。若い心の愛しさと愚かさから、外套も傘もなく霧雨の中を四マイル歩いたあとで、しかも疲れるだろうから来なくていいという恋人の言葉にもかかわらず、彼はただ彼女のそばに十分間いたいという一心で、わざわざこの一マイルをまた遠回りしてきたのだった。
parts: in the fondness and foolishness of his young heart, after walking four miles, in a drizzling rain without overcoat or umbrella, and in face of a remark from his love that he was not to come because he would be tired
to wander this mile out of his way again
from sheer wish of spending ten minutes in her presence
point: it を本当の目的語と思うと、to wander ~ の扱いに困って第3文型を選びやすい。また a remark that he was not to come にもつられる。it は形式目的語で、真の目的語は to wander ~。it＝his business の第5文型。
explanation: make it one’s business to do「わざわざ〜する」。it は to wander を指す仮目的語で、his business が補語。SVOC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ

text: Jopp’s dislike of Farfrae as the man who had once ursurped his place, while it made him a willing tool, made him, at the same time, commercially as unsafe a colleague as Henchard could have chosen.
translation: かつて自分の地位を奪った男としてファーフレイを嫌うジョップの気持ちは、彼を進んで使える道具にはしたが、同時に、ヘンチャードが選びうる仲間のうちで、商売の上では最も危なっかしい相棒にもしていた。
parts: as the man who had once ursurped his place, while it made him a willing tool
commercially as unsafe a colleague as Henchard could have chosen
point: as unsafe a colleague as ~ の比較の形や、while 節の made him a willing tool に気を取られやすい。補語は as 〜 as の名詞句全体。make O C で、him＝colleague の第5文型。
explanation: make O C「O を C にする」。him と as unsafe a colleague ... が O と C。SVOC。
author: Thomas Hardy
authorJa: トマス・ハーディ
workJa: カスターブリッジの市長
