text: That fine old lady herself was worth driving ten miles to see, any day; her beauty, her well-preserved faculties, and her old-fashioned dignity made her a graceful subject for conversation in turn with the King’s health, the sweet new patterns in cotton dresses, the news from Egypt, and Lord Dacey’s lawsuit, which was fretting poor Lady Dacey to death.
target: her beauty, her well-preserved faculties, and her old-fashioned dignity made her a graceful subject for conversation in turn with the King’s health, the sweet new patterns in cotton dresses, the news from Egypt, and Lord Dacey’s lawsuit, which was fretting poor Lady Dacey to death
translation: あの立派な老婦人は、いつだって十マイル車を走らせて会いに行くだけの値打ちがあった。その美しさ、よく保たれた頭の働き、古風な威厳のおかげで、彼女は国王のご容体や新しい木綿服のかわいい柄、エジプトからの知らせ、ダシー夫人を死ぬほど気をもませているダシー卿の訴訟などと並んで、交互に語られる上品な話題になっていた。
parts: her beauty, her well-preserved faculties, and her old-fashioned dignity
in turn with the King’s health, the sweet new patterns in cotton dresses, the news from Egypt, and Lord Dacey’s lawsuit, which was fretting poor Lady Dacey to death
point: 前半の was worth driving ten miles to see や lawsuit, which was fretting ~ に気を取られ、主語が3つ並ぶので動詞を見失いやすい。make O C で、her＝a graceful subject。第5文型。
explanation: make O C で、her と a graceful subject が O と C。判定部分は SVOC。
author: George Eliot
authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット

text: This was what he added in the interview, and by the time he had got Lapham past the period where risen Americans are all pathetically alike in their narrow circumstances, their sufferings, and their aspirations, he had beguiled him into forgetfulness of the check he had received, and had him talking again in perfect enjoyment of his autobiography.
target: he had beguiled him into forgetfulness of the check he had received, and had him talking again in perfect enjoyment of his autobiography
translation: これが面談で彼が付け加えたことだった。そして、成り上がったアメリカ人がだれも哀れなほど似ている時期――狭い境遇、苦しみ、望み――をラパムに語り終えさせたころには、彼はラパムを言いくるめて、受けた冷たい仕打ちを忘れさせ、ふたたび自分の身の上話をすっかり楽しんで語らせていた。
parts: into forgetfulness of the check he had received
in perfect enjoyment of his autobiography
point: 前半の beguiled him into forgetfulness（SVO＋前置詞句）を見て第3文型を選びやすい。しかし続く had him talking again は have O -ing（O に〜させておく）で、him＝talking。第5文型。
explanation: have O -ing「O に〜させておく」。him と talking again が O と C。SVOC（前半の beguile O into 〜 は SVO＋M）。
author: William Dean Howells
authorJa: W・D・ハウエルズ
workJa: サイラス・ラパムの出世

text: But, like all beliefs not genuinely held, this one depended very much upon the amount of acceptance it received from other people, and in private, when the pressure of public opinion was removed, Ralph let himself swing very rapidly away from his actual circumstances upon strange voyages which, indeed, he would have been ashamed to describe.
target: Ralph let himself swing very rapidly away from his actual circumstances upon strange voyages which, indeed, he would have been ashamed to describe
translation: しかし、本気で抱いているのではない信念がみなそうであるように、この信念も、ほかの人々にどれだけ受け入れられるかに大きく左右された。人前ではなく一人になって、世間の目の圧力が取り除かれると、ラルフは自分の実際の境遇からすばやく離れ、奇妙な航海へとわが身をさまよわせた。それはじっさい、人に話すのは恥ずかしいような航海だった。
parts: very rapidly away from his actual circumstances upon strange voyages which, indeed, he would have been ashamed to describe
point: let を「〜させる」の使役と気づかず、swing を名詞や修飾語と見て第3文型を選びやすい。また後半の関係詞節にもつられる。使役の let＋O＋原形で、himself が swing する関係。第5文型。
explanation: let O 原形「O に〜させておく」。himself と swing が O と C。SVOC。
author: Virginia Woolf
authorJa: ヴァージニア・ウルフ

text: Poor Mr. Harding felt himself completely snubbed, and of course said nothing further; but Mr. Arabin, who had yielded submissively in the small matters of the cellar and kitchen grate, found himself obliged to oppose reforms which might be of a nature too expensive for his pocket.
translation: 気の毒なハーディング氏は、すっかりはねつけられたと感じ、当然それ以上は何も言わなかった。しかしアラビン氏は、酒蔵や台所の炉格子といった小さなことでは素直に譲ったものの、自分のふところには高くつきすぎるかもしれない改革には反対せざるをえないと感じた。
parts: who had yielded submissively in the small matters of the cellar and kitchen grate
obliged to oppose reforms which might be of a nature too expensive for his pocket
point: 途中の said nothing further（SVO）を見て第3文型を選びやすい。また who had yielded ~ の関係詞節も長い。felt himself snubbed と found himself obliged to oppose ~ がともに O＝C の関係。第5文型。
explanation: feel oneself C「自分が〜だと感じる」、find oneself C「自分が〜だとわかる」。SVOC が2つ（間の said nothing は SVO）。
author: Anthony Trollope
authorJa: アントニー・トロロープ
